title: Palivizumab for respiratory syncytial virus immunoprophylaxis in high-risk populations in Qatar: a call for action
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Preterm and high-risk infants are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, leading to prolonged hospitalization, intensive care unit admissions, respiratory support and death. Although, RSV prevention is a major health priority in Qatar, national guidelines for RSV prophylaxis are currently lacking. AREAS COVERED: This expert opinion summarizes the burden of RSV in Qatar and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) along with current immunoprophylaxis practices and real-world evidence on the effectiveness of palivizumab in high-risk infants. Evidence from a literature review was supplemented by expert insights relevant to Qatar and the GCC to address data gaps and heterogeneity in RSV prophylaxis. The integrated findings support context-specific recommendations. EXPERT OPINION: A steering committee with 16 experts was convened in December 2024 to review the available evidence and discuss challenges in RSV prevention among high-risk infants in Qatar. The experts reviewed the literature and reached consensus for the recommendations. This paper provides a localized, evidence-based action plan for the healthcare community, while facilitating optimal utilization of resources and cost-effective practices for RSV prophylaxis in Qatar. It also acknowledges the necessity to collaborate with other GCC countries and develop a regional protocol to further strengthen the RSV prevention efforts.

title: Respiratory syncytial virus infection in COPD exacerbations: the RECODE study protocol.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often suffer episodes of exacerbation (ECOPD). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an increasingly recognised cause of illness in adults. Yet the prevalence of RSV during ECOPD and its association with clinically relevant outcomes remain insufficiently defined. The RECODE study sought to determine the prevalence of RSV infection in patients with ECOPD and to assess the association between RSV and hospitalisation, length of stay, acute cardiovascular events and/or death. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prospective, multicentre, observational, controlled (RSV-positive cases vs RSV-negative controls), longitudinal study (NCT06735612). Adults ≥50 years with ECOPD will be enrolled at urgent-care presentation (V1), contacted by telephone at day 15 (V2) and seen in the clinic at 3 months (V3). RSV status will be determined by Reverse Transcription (RT-PCR) on nasopharyngeal swabs; additional measures include paired serology, routine clinical data, spirometry at V3 and predefined outcomes. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The leading Ethics Committee was that of Clinic Barcelona (HCB/2024/0771). All participating centres accepted this approval or requested local approval from their respective Institutional Review Boards (Appendix). Results will be disseminated in international publications and meeting presentations as well as in a plain language summary to be distributed among participating patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06735612.

abstract_zh: 简介:慢性阻塞性肺疾病(COPD)患者经常会出现病情加重(ECOPD)。呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是一种日益被认可的成人疾病病因。然而,ECOPD 期间 RSV 的 患病率 及其与临床相关结果的关联仍未得到充分定义。RECODE 研究旨在确定 ECOPD 患者 RSV 感染的 患病率,并评估 RSV 与住院、住院时间、急性心血管事件和/或死亡之间的关联。方法和分析:前瞻性、多中心、观察性、对照(RSV 阳性病例与 RSV 阴性对照)、纵向研究 (NCT06735612)。≥50 岁患有 ECOPD 的成年人将参加紧急护理就诊 (V1),在第 15 天通过电话联系 (V2),并在 3 个月时到诊所就诊 (V3)。RSV 状态将通过鼻咽拭子的逆转录 (RT-PCR) 来确定;其他措施包括配对 血清学、常规临床数据、V3 肺活量测定和预定义结果。道德与传播:主要的道德委员会是巴塞罗那诊所的道德委员会 (HCB/2024/0771)。所有参与中心均接受此批准或请求各自机构审查委员会的当地批准(附录)。结果将在国际出版物和会议演示文稿中以及以通俗易懂的语言摘要的形式传播给参与的患者。试用注册号:NCT06735612。

title: Maternal Immunization Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus: An Integrative Review of Efficacy, Safety, and Implementation
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infection in young infants and accounts for substantial morbidity, hospitalization, and mortality worldwide, with the highest burden concentrated in the first months of life, when immunological and anatomical immaturity favors severe disease. Maternal vaccination has emerged as a strategy to bridge this window of vulnerability through the transplacental transfer of neutralizing antibodies. This integrative review synthesizes scientific articles published between 2022 and 2026, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, and position statements from national and international scientific societies, addressing the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, mechanism of action, efficacy, safety, and public health impact of maternal RSV immunization. The bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF; Abrysvo®), administered as a single intramuscular dose between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation, induces maternal IgG that is transferred to the fetus and confers passive protection during the first six months of life. In the phase 3 MATISSE trial, vaccination demonstrated 81.8% efficacy against severe RSV lower respiratory tract infection within 90 days of birth and 69.4% within 180 days, alongside reductions in hospitalization. The safety profile was favorable, with predominantly mild and transient adverse events; a numerical imbalance in preterm birth remains under surveillance and underlies the precautionary gestational window. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab) are best regarded as complementary rather than competing strategies. Current evidence supports maternal immunization as one of the most effective measures to reduce the burden of RSV disease in early infancy.

title_zh: 针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 的孕产妇免疫:有效性、安全性和实施的综合审查
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infection in young infants and accounts for substantial morbidity, hospitalization, and mortality worldwide, with the highest burden concentrated in the first months of life, when immunological and anatomical immaturity favors severe disease. Maternal vaccination has emerged as a strategy to bridge this window of vulnerability through the transplacental transfer of neutralizing antibodies. This integrative review synthesizes scientific articles published between 2022 and 2026, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, and position statements from national and international scientific societies, addressing the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, mechanism of action, efficacy, safety, and public health impact of maternal RSV immunization. The bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF; Abrysvo®), administered as a single intramuscular dose between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation, induces maternal IgG that is transferred to the fetus and confers passive protection during the first six months of life. In the phase 3 MATISSE trial, vaccination demonstrated 81.8% efficacy against severe RSV lower respiratory tract infection within 90 days of birth and 69.4% within 180 days, alongside reductions in hospitalization. The safety profile was favorable, with predominantly mild and transient adverse events; a numerical imbalance in preterm birth remains under surveillance and underlies the precautionary gestational window. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab) are best regarded as complementary rather than competing strategies. Current evidence supports maternal immunization as one of the most effective measures to reduce the burden of RSV disease in early infancy.

title: Modulation of Respiratory Diseases by the Endocannabinoid System: A Therapeutic Perspective.
abstract: Respiratory system diseases represent a major global health burden, characterized by high prevalence and significant morbidity and mortality. The respiratory tract's direct and continuous exposure to the external environment makes it particularly vulnerable to pathogens, pollutants and other injurious agents. This exposure often triggers excessive inflammatory responses and compromises the integrity of the air-blood barrier, leading to impaired gas exchange, hypoxia and respiratory failure. Therefore, modulating pulmonary inflammation and enhancing barrier function are critical therapeutic objectives. The endocannabinoid system, a ubiquitous signalling network comprising cannabinoid receptors, endogenous ligands and metabolic enzymes, has emerged as a crucial modulator of these processes. This review summarizes the role of the ECS in major respiratory diseases, including asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection and acute lung injury. The evidence highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the ECS through strategies such as receptor-specific ligands and inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes. However, the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation necessitates precise intervention. Future efforts should focus on developing selective therapeutics and validating their efficacy in clinical settings, positioning the ECS as a sophisticated target for innovative respiratory disease management.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of the endocannabinoid system (ECS) in modulating respiratory diseases, focusing on its therapeutic potential for conditions such as asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection, and acute lung injury. The central question addresses how ECS modulation—via receptor-specific ligands or inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes—could mitigate excessive pulmonary inflammation and restore air-blood barrier integrity to improve gas exchange and reduce respiratory failure.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review summarizing the ECS's involvement in respiratory diseases without explicit systematic search methods, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The review synthesizes evidence on ECS modulation strategies but does not report databases searched, search dates, or a meta-analysis process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the ECS is a critical modulator of pulmonary inflammation and barrier function, with therapeutic potential in respiratory diseases. It highlights the need for precise ECS-targeted interventions due to the system's context-dependent effects, emphasizing receptor-specific ligands and enzyme inhibitors as promising strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation as a key unresolved issue, complicating the development of universally effective therapeutics. It also notes the lack of clinical validation for ECS-targeted strategies in respiratory diseases, leaving mechanisms and efficacy in human populations insufficiently characterized.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of selective ECS therapeutics and their validation in clinical settings to establish efficacy and safety. It also calls for mechanistic studies to clarify the context-dependent effects of ECS modulation in respiratory diseases, ensuring targeted and effective interventions.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,ECS 是肺部炎症和屏障功能的关键调节剂,具有治疗呼吸系统疾病的潜力。它强调了由于系统的上下文相关效应而需要精确的 ECS 靶向干预措施,并强调受体特异性配体和酶抑制剂是有前途的策略。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of the endocannabinoid system (ECS) in modulating respiratory diseases, focusing on its therapeutic potential for conditions such as asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection, and acute lung injury. The central question addresses how ECS modulation—via receptor-specific ligands or inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes—could mitigate excessive pulmonary inflammation and restore air-blood barrier integrity to improve gas exchange and reduce respiratory failure.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review summarizing the ECS's involvement in respiratory diseases without explicit systematic search methods, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The review synthesizes evidence on ECS modulation strategies but does not report databases searched, search dates, or a meta-analysis process.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the ECS is a critical modulator of pulmonary inflammation and barrier function, with therapeutic potential in respiratory diseases. It highlights the need for precise ECS-targeted interventions due to the system's context-dependent effects, emphasizing receptor-specific ligands and enzyme inhibitors as promising strategies.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation as a key unresolved issue, complicating the development of universally effective therapeutics. It also notes the lack of clinical validation for ECS-targeted strategies in respiratory diseases, leaving mechanisms and efficacy in human populations insufficiently characterized.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of selective ECS therapeutics and their validation in clinical settings to establish efficacy and safety. It also calls for mechanistic studies to clarify the context-dependent effects of ECS modulation in respiratory diseases, ensuring targeted and effective interventions.

title_zh: 内源性大麻素系统调节呼吸系统疾病:治疗视角。
source_body_en: Respiratory system diseases represent a major global health burden, characterized by high prevalence and significant morbidity and mortality. The respiratory tract's direct and continuous exposure to the external environment makes it particularly vulnerable to pathogens, pollutants and other injurious agents. This exposure often triggers excessive inflammatory responses and compromises the integrity of the air-blood barrier, leading to impaired gas exchange, hypoxia and respiratory failure. Therefore, modulating pulmonary inflammation and enhancing barrier function are critical therapeutic objectives. The endocannabinoid system, a ubiquitous signalling network comprising cannabinoid receptors, endogenous ligands and metabolic enzymes, has emerged as a crucial modulator of these processes. This review summarizes the role of the ECS in major respiratory diseases, including asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory syncytial virus infection and acute lung injury. The evidence highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting the ECS through strategies such as receptor-specific ligands and inhibitors of endocannabinoid-degrading enzymes. However, the context-dependent nature of ECS modulation necessitates precise intervention. Future efforts should focus on developing selective therapeutics and validating their efficacy in clinical settings, positioning the ECS as a sophisticated target for innovative respiratory disease management.

title: Association between educational level and acceptance of antenatal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination among Saudi women: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction Recently, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine was approved and recommended for pregnant women in Saudi Arabia. Data are needed regarding pregnant women's awareness of RSV infection and their acceptance of the RSV vaccine. Therefore, in this study, we aimed to assess the awareness and acceptance of antenatal RSV vaccines among postpartum women in Al-Madinah, Saudi Arabia. Methods This hospital-based, cross-sectional study was conducted at two hospitals in Al-Madinah, Saudi Arabia. A validated 13-item questionnaire was used, including questions regarding demographic data, awareness of RSV infection, and acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine. Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between demographic data and awareness and acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine. Results Among 400 postpartum women (mean age, 30 years; range, 18–44 years), 51% were aware of RSV infection. Most provided correct answers regarding the mode of RSV transmission (72.5%). Approximately 40% of the participants perceived the seriousness of the RSV infection to be high for infants after delivery. Acceptance for receiving the RSV vaccine was moderate (58%). Compared with high school or lower educational level, university or higher education was associated with lower acceptance of the RSV vaccine (odds ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval, 0.56–0.93). Conclusions Despite moderate awareness of RSV infection, maternal acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine among highly educated women was lower than that among women with a lower education level. This low acceptance rate highlights the need for future studies to evaluate the actual uptake of antenatal RSV vaccination among highly educated women.

title_zh: 沙特妇女教育水平与产前 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 接受度之间的关联:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Introduction Recently, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine was approved and recommended for pregnant women in Saudi Arabia. Data are needed regarding pregnant women's awareness of RSV infection and their acceptance of the RSV vaccine. Therefore, in this study, we aimed to assess the awareness and acceptance of antenatal RSV vaccines among postpartum women in Al-Madinah, Saudi Arabia. Methods This hospital-based, cross-sectional study was conducted at two hospitals in Al-Madinah, Saudi Arabia. A validated 13-item questionnaire was used, including questions regarding demographic data, awareness of RSV infection, and acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine. Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between demographic data and awareness and acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine. Results Among 400 postpartum women (mean age, 30 years; range, 18–44 years), 51% were aware of RSV infection. Most provided correct answers regarding the mode of RSV transmission (72.5%). Approximately 40% of the participants perceived the seriousness of the RSV infection to be high for infants after delivery. Acceptance for receiving the RSV vaccine was moderate (58%). Compared with high school or lower educational level, university or higher education was associated with lower acceptance of the RSV vaccine (odds ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval, 0.56–0.93). Conclusions Despite moderate awareness of RSV infection, maternal acceptance of the antenatal RSV vaccine among highly educated women was lower than that among women with a lower education level. This low acceptance rate highlights the need for future studies to evaluate the actual uptake of antenatal RSV vaccination among highly educated women.

title: Screening and mechanism analysis of core target genes for resveratrol inhibiting respiratory syncytial virus.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus, is a major pathogen of acute respiratory tract infections, posing severe threats to the health of infants, the elderly and immunocompromised individuals. While approved vaccines for older adults and monoclonal antibody prophylaxis for infants are available, effective therapeutic drugs remain scarce. Resveratrol, a phenolic compound naturally present in grapes, berries and other foods, has been confirmed to exhibit anti-RSV activity, but its molecular mechanism of action remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to screen the core targets and key signaling pathways of resveratrol against RSV using computational biology approaches, propose testable research hypotheses and provide a theoretical basis for subsequent experimental validation. METHODS: A total of 261 resveratrol-related targets and 1196 RSV-related targets were retrieved from databases. Venny 2.1.0 was used to identify 67 overlapping targets, which were then subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction via STRING/Cytoscape and topological analysis for core target screening. GO/KEGG enrichment analyses were performed using the DAVID database and molecular docking validation was conducted with PyMOL/AutoDock. RESULTS: Ten core targets including EGFR, SRC, HSP90AA1 and ALB were identified. GO enrichment focused on biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathways were enriched in the Ras signaling pathway and others. Molecular docking showed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies <-5 kcal/mol. CONCLUSION: This in-silico study predicts that resveratrol may exert anti-RSV effects by targeting host proteins such as EGFR and SRC and regulating key pathways including PI3K-Akt and Ras, complementing existing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. The study provides novel insights for anti-RSV drug development and a theoretical foundation for subsequent experimental validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe acute respiratory infections in vulnerable populations, and despite available vaccines and prophylaxis, effective therapeutic drugs remain limited. The study was needed to clarify the molecular mechanism by which resveratrol, a natural phenolic compound with reported anti-RSV activity, exerts its effects.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This in-silico study screened core target genes and signaling pathways of resveratrol against RSV using computational biology approaches. It integrated 261 resveratrol-related targets and 1196 RSV-related targets from public databases to identify overlapping targets and perform network and pathway analyses.
analysis.methods: Overlapping targets were identified using Venny 2.1.0, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction via STRING/Cytoscape and topological analysis to screen core targets. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed using the DAVID database, and molecular docking validation was conducted with PyMOL/AutoDock to assess binding stability.
analysis.main_results: Ten core targets including EGFR, SRC, HSP90AA1 and ALB were identified. GO enrichment highlighted biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathways were enriched in the Ras signaling pathway and others. Molecular docking showed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies below -5 kcal/mol.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that resveratrol may inhibit RSV by targeting host proteins such as EGFR and SRC and modulating key pathways including PI3K-Akt and Ras, complementing existing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. It provides novel insights for anti-RSV drug development and a theoretical foundation for experimental validation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential host-targeted therapeutic strategies for RSV using resveratrol, offering a mechanistic basis for future antiviral drug development and experimental studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As an in-silico study, the evidence is limited by the lack of in vitro or in vivo validation, which constrains the strength of causal inference and generalizability. The confidence in the findings is therefore assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This in-silico study investigated the molecular mechanism by which resveratrol may inhibit respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) by screening core target genes and signaling pathways. GO enrichment highlighted biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathway analysis enriched the Ras signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies below -5 kcal/mol. The study interprets that resveratrol may exert anti-RSV effects by targeting host proteins and modulating key pathways, complementing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. While the findings provide novel insights and a theoretical foundation for anti-RSV drug development, the lack of in vitro or in vivo validation limits causal inference and generalizability, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title_zh: 白藜芦醇抑制呼吸道合胞病毒核心靶基因筛选及机制分析
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus, is a major pathogen of acute respiratory tract infections, posing severe threats to the health of infants, the elderly and immunocompromised individuals. While approved vaccines for older adults and monoclonal antibody prophylaxis for infants are available, effective therapeutic drugs remain scarce. Resveratrol, a phenolic compound naturally present in grapes, berries and other foods, has been confirmed to exhibit anti-RSV activity, but its molecular mechanism of action remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to screen the core targets and key signaling pathways of resveratrol against RSV using computational biology approaches, propose testable research hypotheses and provide a theoretical basis for subsequent experimental validation. METHODS: A total of 261 resveratrol-related targets and 1196 RSV-related targets were retrieved from databases. Venny 2.1.0 was used to identify 67 overlapping targets, which were then subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction via STRING/Cytoscape and topological analysis for core target screening. GO/KEGG enrichment analyses were performed using the DAVID database and molecular docking validation was conducted with PyMOL/AutoDock. RESULTS: Ten core targets including EGFR, SRC, HSP90AA1 and ALB were identified. GO enrichment focused on biological processes such as PI3K-Akt signal transduction and MAPK cascade regulation, while KEGG pathways were enriched in the Ras signaling pathway and others. Molecular docking showed stable binding of resveratrol to core targets, with all binding energies <-5 kcal/mol. CONCLUSION: This in-silico study predicts that resveratrol may exert anti-RSV effects by targeting host proteins such as EGFR and SRC and regulating key pathways including PI3K-Akt and Ras, complementing existing evidence of its direct interaction with viral proteins. The study provides novel insights for anti-RSV drug development and a theoretical foundation for subsequent experimental validation.

title: Infant respiratory syncytial virus and childhood asthma: a nationwide registry-based, sibling-controlled, and genome-wide association study
abstract: BackgroundEarly-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection is associated with childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), but causality and shared genetic liability remain unclear. MethodsWe combined Finnish nationwide registries and Nordic genetic cohorts. First, in 965 312 Finnish children born between 1998 and 2014, we defined severe RSV as RSV hospitalisation before age 1 year, and recurrent wheezing or asthma (RW/A) as inhaled medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years, and compared medication and eosinophil trajectories by RSV history. Second, we assessed familial confounding in 527 776 full siblings and 15 667 RW/A- discordant pairs. Third, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of RSV susceptibility with meta-analysis across six Nordic cohorts (3 107 cases, 92 091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. FindingsRSV-associated RW/A showed higher inhaled medication use at ages 1-2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0{middle dot}341 vs 0{middle dot}398x10{square}/L; p=0{middle dot}008) than RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. In RW/A-discordant sibling pairs, RSV hospitalisation was associated with RW/A (OR 2{middle dot}8; 95% CI 2{middle dot}4-3{middle dot}2), while unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; {beta}=0{middle dot}209; p=8{middle dot}80x10-{square}). 2SMR provided no evidence that asthma genetic liability influenced RSV susceptibility. InterpretationThe RSV-asthma association is unlikely to be explained by shared genetic or environmental factors, and RSV-associated RW/A shows a distinct trajectory. These findings help prioritise long-term outcomes for RSV prevention trials and monitoring. FundingPaivikki and Sakari Sohlberg Foundation, Foundation for Pediatric Research, Sigrid Juselius Foundation, Orion Research Foundation, the Research Council of Norway.

source_records.abstract: Background Early-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection is associated with childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), but causality and shared genetic liability remain unclear. Methods We combined Finnish nationwide registries and Nordic genetic cohorts. First, in 965 312 Finnish children born between 1998 and 2014, we defined severe RSV as RSV hospitalisation before age 1 year, and recurrent wheezing or asthma (RW/A) as inhaled medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years, and compared medication and eosinophil trajectories by RSV history. Second, we assessed familial confounding in 527 776 full siblings and 15 667 RW/A-discordant pairs. Third, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of RSV susceptibility with meta-analysis across six Nordic cohorts (3 107 cases, 92 031 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; beta=0.209; p=8.80*10e-9). 2SMR provided no evidence that asthma genetic liability influenced RSV susceptibility. Interpretation The RSV-asthma association is unlikely to be explained by shared genetic or environmental factors, and RSV-associated RW/A shows a distinct trajectory. These findings help prioritise long-term outcomes for RSV prevention trials and monitoring. title_original: Infant respiratory syncytial virus and childhood asthma: a nationwide registry-based, sibling-controlled, and genome-wide association study

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether early-life respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection causes childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A), focusing on causality, shared genetic liability, and distinct clinical trajectories. The central question addresses the association between severe RSV infection (hospitalisation before age 1 year) and RW/A (medication reimbursement between ages 1 and 7 years) in a nationwide registry-based cohort.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes evidence from a nationwide registry-based study in Finland (1998–2014) combining registry data with Nordic genetic cohorts. It includes a genome-wide association study (GWAS) across six Nordic cohorts (3,107 cases, 92,091 controls) and two-sample Mendelian randomisation (2SMR) using 155 asthma-associated variants. The review does not explicitly report eligibility criteria, search dates, or databases beyond the described cohorts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that RSV-associated RW/A exhibits distinct clinical features, including higher inhaled medication use at ages 1–2 years but lower use after age 5, and lower mean blood eosinophils (0.341 vs 0.398 x109/L; p=0.008) compared to RW/A without RSV hospitalisation. Sibling-controlled analyses show an association between RSV hospitalisation and RW/A (OR 2.8; 95% CI 2.4–3.2), though unaffected siblings also had elevated RW/A prevalence. GWAS identified an RSV association at APBB1IP (rs787036; β=0.209; p=8.80x10−8), and 2SMR found no evidence that asthma genetic liability influences RSV susceptibility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved questions about the causal pathway between RSV and RW/A, as sibling analyses suggest potential unmeasured confounding despite familial controls. The distinct eosinophil trajectory in RSV-associated RW/A remains mechanistically unexplained, and the GWAS signal at APBB1IP requires further validation and functional studies to clarify its role in RSV susceptibility.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritises long-term outcome monitoring in RSV prevention trials to assess whether reducing severe RSV infections mitigates RW/A risk. It also calls for mechanistic studies to elucidate the eosinophil trajectory differences and functional validation of the APBB1IP locus to determine its biological relevance to RSV susceptibility.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the association between early-life severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection and childhood recurrent wheeze or asthma (RW/A) using nationwide registry data, sibling-controlled analyses, and genetic studies. Key findings include distinct clinical trajectories in RSV-associated RW/A, such as higher early medication use but lower eosinophil levels, and an association with RW/A in sibling analyses (OR 2.8). A genome-wide association study identified a potential RSV susceptibility locus (APBB1IP), while Mendelian randomisation found no shared genetic liability between asthma and RSV. Unresolved questions include the causal pathway, confounding in sibling analyses, and the mechanistic basis of eosinophil differences. The review prioritises long-term monitoring in RSV prevention trials and mechanistic studies to validate genetic findings and clarify causality.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了生命早期的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染是否会导致儿童反复喘息或哮喘 (RW/A),重点关注因果关系、共同的遗传倾向和不同的临床轨迹。核心问题是在基于全国登记的 队列研究 中解决严重 RSV 感染(1 岁之前住院)和 RW/A(1 岁至 7 岁之间的药物报销)之间的关联。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了芬兰一项全国性登记研究(1998-2014 年)的证据,该研究将登记数据与北欧遗传 队列研究 相结合。它包括一项针对六个北欧 队列研究(3,107 例病例,92,091 名对照)的 基因组 全关联研究 (GWAS) 和使用 155 种哮喘相关变异的两样本孟德尔随机化 (2SMR)。审查没有明确报告资格标准、检索日期或超出所描述的 队列研究 的数据库。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,与没有 RSV 住院的 RW/A 相比,RSV 相关的 RW/A 表现出独特的临床特征,包括 1-2 岁时吸入药物使用量较高,但 5 岁后使用量较低,平均血液嗜酸性粒细胞较低(0.341 vs 0.398 x109/L;p=0.008)。兄弟姐妹对照分析显示 RSV 住院治疗与 RW/A 之间存在关联(OR 2.8;95% CI 2.4-3.2),尽管未受影响的兄弟姐妹的 RW/A 患病率 也升高。GWAS 在 APBB1IP 上发现了 RSV 关联(rs787036;β=0.209;p=8.80x10−8),并且 2SMR 没有发现证据表明哮喘遗传倾向影响 RSV 易感性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了有关 RSV 和 RW/A 之间因果关系的尚未解决的问题,因为兄弟姐妹分析表明,尽管有家族控制,但仍存在潜在的未测量的混杂因素。RSV 相关 RW/A 中独特的嗜酸性粒细胞轨迹在机制上仍然无法解释,APBB1IP 上的 GWAS 信号需要进一步验证和功能研究,以阐明其在 RSV 易感性中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑 RSV 预防试验中的长期结果监测,以评估减少严重 RSV 感染是否可以减轻 RW/A 风险。它还需要进行机制研究来阐明嗜酸性粒细胞轨迹差异,并对 APBB1IP 基因座进行功能验证,以确定其与 RSV 易感性的生物学相关性。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑 RSV 预防试验中的长期结果监测,以评估减少严重 RSV 感染是否可以减轻 RW/A 风险。它还需要进行机制研究来阐明嗜酸性粒细胞轨迹差异,并对 APBB1IP 基因座进行功能验证,以确定其与 RSV 易感性的生物学相关性。

title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children. Data on their molecular epidemiology in northern India remains limited, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. RESULTS: A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒是儿童严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的主要原因,但其分子 流行病学 在印度北部,特别是在 COVID-19 大流行之后,仍然没有充分记录。本研究通过调查克什米尔住院儿科 SARI 患者中的 患病率 和呼吸道病毒病原体的分布来解决知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 10 月至 2025 年 4 月在斯利那加谢尔克什米尔医学科学研究所进行了一项前瞻性研究。纳入符合世界卫生组织SARI病例定义的年龄≤15岁的儿童,总共有326例儿童SARI病例。
elements_zh.methods: 收集鼻咽和/或口咽样本,并使用实时聚合酶链反应检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A 和 B、腺病毒、人类偏肺病毒、鼻病毒和副流感病毒。
elements_zh.main_results: 200 名患者(61.3%)中至少检测到一种呼吸道病毒。RSV 是最常检测到的病毒,其中 RSV-B 在 111 例(34.0%)中检出,RSV-A 在 26 例(7.9%)中检出。流感病毒所占比例较小,其中甲型H1N1流感12例(3.6%),甲型H3N2流感6例(1.8%),乙型流感(维多利亚系)21例(6.4%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,克什米尔儿童严重急性呼吸道感染病例中呼吸道病毒占很大比例,RSV 成为大流行后时期的主要病原体。这一发现与大流行前的模式形成鲜明对比,并强调需要更新 监测 策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 加强分子 监测 可以改善诊断管理并指导该地区儿科 SARI 的有针对性的预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其单中心设计和缺乏纵向随访而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性和时间趋势。由于基于医院的 队列研究 缺乏对照和潜在的选择偏倚,证据强度中等。

title: NonPharmaceutical Interventions and PostPandemic Resurgence: The Shifting Epidemiology of Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus, and Adenovirus in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province (2020-2024)
abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections (ARIs) caused by influenza A/B (Flu A/Flu B), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and adenovirus (ADV) remain a major global health burden. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered respiratory virus transmission through nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs). Methods Samples from patients with respiratory tract infections at Hangzhou Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2020 to October 2024 were collected. ADV, Flu A, Flu B, and RSV were detected to evaluate the impact of NPIs on viral epidemiology. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software and GraphPad Prism. Multivariable binary logistic regression models, adjusting for age group and sex, were constructed to evaluate the independent effect of NPI relaxation (strict NPI period 2020-2022 vs. post-relaxation period 2023-2024) on virus positivity. Stratified analyses by age group and demographic comparability assessments between periods were also performed. Results Overall virus positivity declined from 27.4% (2020) to 14.5% (2021) during strict NPIs, then rebounded to 35.1% in 2023 after relaxation. Flu A resurged atypically in summer 2022 and dominated the 2023 winter peak, while Flu B increased annually and peaked in 2024. ADV regained its prepandemic summer seasonality by 2024, whereas RSV showed limited seasonal variation. Higher ADV positivity was observed in males, and higher Flu B positivity in females. By 2024, influenza burden shifted toward adults and geriatric populations, while children under five remained most vulnerable to RSV and ADV. However, after adjusting for demographic shifts—including a significant increase in adult patients (18-60 years: 22.1% to 40.0%) and altered sex ratios between periods (both P 0.05). Stratified analyses further revealed that the magnitude of period-related risk reduction increased with age for all pathogens. Conclusion This study demonstrates that the postpandemic resurgence of respiratory viruses in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, was not a monolithic recrudescence following NPIs relaxation, but a multifaceted shifting epidemiology driven by three convergent forces: expanded school-based and community screening that broadened the tested denominator, demographic case-mix shifts toward higher-risk adult populations, and pathogen-specific alterations in seasonal and age-specific transmission patterns. The consistently lower adjusted odds of positivity during the post-relaxation period indicate that crude resurgence signals must be interpreted through the lens of surveillance structure.

title: Comparison of the protective effect of human respiratory syncytial virus Pre-F protein combined with different adjuvants in BALB/c mice
abstract: Introduction Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) has a high disease burden in infants and elderly individuals. In this study, the adjuvants AlOH, AlOH+CpG and BFA03 were used to compare the protective effect of HRSV prefusion protein (Pre-F) in BALB/c mice. Methods We divided BALB/c mice into three experimental groups (Pre-F+AlOH+CpG, Pre-F+AlOH, and Pre-F+BFA03) and three adjuvant control groups (AlOH+CpG, AlOH, and BFA03). After two intramuscular immunizations, we measured serum neutralizing antibody titers and quantified the numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. After viral challenge, we monitored body weight changes, determined lung viral loads (Ct values), and scored lung pathological damage. Results The mice in the experimental groups exhibited high titres of neutralizing antibodies and increased numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. The mice began to regain weight on the third day after challenge, but the mice in the adjuvant groups continued to lose weight. The mice immunized with Pre-F+BFA03 elicited the highest neutralizing antibody titre (1716), the lowest viral load in the lung, and milder pathological damage. The mice immunized with Pre-F+AlOH had the most severe lung pathological injury (score: 2.83) and the highest viral load in the lung (Ct value: 32.2). Compared with the BFA03 adjuvant, the AlOH adjuvant induced a Th2-biased humoral immune response in mice. The Pre-F+AlOH+CpG group had the least pathological damage in the lung (score 2.16), and the ability to induce neutralizing antibodies and cellular immune responses was comparable with that of the BFA03 adjuvant. Discussion These findings indicate that Pre-F protein combined with AlOH+CpG or BFA03 adjuvant provided similar protection in mice and both were superior to the AlOH adjuvant, providing a reference for adjuvant selection and formulation strategies in HRSV Pre-F protein vaccine development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) imposes a substantial disease burden in infants and elderly individuals, creating an unmet need for more effective vaccines. The study aimed to determine which adjuvant combination with HRSV prefusion protein (Pre-F) elicits the strongest protective immune response in a mouse model.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used BALB/c mice immunized with HRSV Pre-F protein combined with three adjuvants (AlOH, AlOH+CpG, BFA03) and corresponding adjuvant-only controls. Mice were divided into six groups and received two intramuscular immunizations before viral challenge.
analysis.methods: Serum neutralizing antibody titers were measured, and the numbers of IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes were quantified. After challenge, body weight changes, lung viral loads (Ct values), and lung pathological damage were assessed.
analysis.main_results: Mice in the experimental groups showed high neutralizing antibody titers and increased IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting lymphocytes. The Pre-F+BFA03 group had the highest neutralizing antibody titer (1716), the lowest lung viral load, and milder pathological damage. The Pre-F+AlOH group exhibited the most severe lung injury (score: 2.83) and highest viral load (Ct: 32.2). The Pre-F+AlOH+CpG group had the least pathological damage (score: 2.16) and comparable immune responses to BFA03.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that Pre-F combined with AlOH+CpG or BFA03 provided similar protection in mice and outperformed AlOH alone, offering a reference for adjuvant selection in HRSV Pre-F vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that AlOH+CpG and BFA03 adjuvants may enhance the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of HRSV Pre-F protein vaccines, informing future vaccine formulation strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in BALB/c mice, limiting direct translation to humans, and lacked long-term follow-up or broader immunological profiling. The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and absence of human data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the protective effect of HRSV prefusion protein (Pre-F) combined with three adjuvants (AlOH, AlOH+CpG, BFA03) in BALB/c mice. Mice were immunized twice intramuscularly and challenged with HRSV, after which neutralizing antibody titers, lymphocyte responses, body weight changes, lung viral loads, and lung pathology were assessed. The Pre-F+BFA03 group showed the highest neutralizing antibody titer (1716), lowest viral load, and mildest pathology, while the Pre-F+AlOH group had the most severe lung injury and highest viral load. The Pre-F+AlOH+CpG group demonstrated minimal lung damage and immune responses comparable to BFA03. The authors conclude that AlOH+CpG and BFA03 adjuvants provide superior protection to AlOH alone, offering guidance for HRSV vaccine development. However, the findings are limited by the mouse model and lack of human validation, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 HRSV Pre-F 蛋白联合三种佐剂(AlOH、AlOH+CpG、BFA03)免疫的 BALB/c 小鼠和相应的仅佐剂对照。将小鼠分为六组,并在病毒攻击前接受两次肌内免疫。
elements_zh.methods: 测量血清中和抗体滴度,并对分泌IFN-γ和IL-4的淋巴细胞的数量进行定量。攻击后,评估体重变化、肺部病毒载量(Ct 值)和肺部病理损伤。
elements_zh.main_results: 实验组中的小鼠表现出高中和抗体滴度,并且分泌 IFN-γ 和 IL-4 的淋巴细胞增多。Pre-F+BFA03组中和抗体滴度最高(1716),肺部病毒载量最低,病理损伤较轻。Pre-F+AlOH 组表现出最严重的肺损伤(评分:2.83)和最高的病毒载量(Ct:32.2)。Pre-F+AlOH+CpG 组的病理损伤最少(评分:2.16),免疫应答 与 BFA03 相当。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,Pre-F 联合 AlOH+CpG 或 BFA03 对小鼠提供了类似的保护作用,并且优于单独使用 AlOH,为 HRSV Pre-F 疫苗 开发中的佐剂选择提供了参考。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明AlOH+CpG和BFA03佐剂可以增强HRSV Pre-F蛋白疫苗的免疫原性和保护功效,为未来的疫苗制剂策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在 BALB/c 小鼠中进行的,限制了直接转化为人类,并且缺乏长期随访或更广泛的免疫学分析。由于样本量小且缺乏人类数据,证据强度中等。

title: Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus nonstructural protein 1 interacts with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 signaling and induce IL-1β
abstract: ABSTRACT Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) caused by PRRS virus (PRRSV) is a highly contagious disease that severely threatens the global pig industry. A significant symptom of PRRS is severe pneumonia. At present, studies have shown that IL-1β is upregulated by PRRSV infection in vivo and in vitro , while the underlying mechanism remains unknown. Here, we explored how PRRSV regulated IL-1β production. We found that HP-PRRSV nsp1 upregulated the expression of IL-1β. Overexpression of nsp1 induced IL-1β production in a dose-dependent manner. Subsequently, we demonstrated that nsp1 enhanced IL-1β expression by activating JNK/p38 signaling pathways, as the addition of p38 and JNK inhibitors reduced IL-1β production induced by nsp1. Moreover, deleting the AP-1 binding motif in porcine IL-1β promoter impaired IL-1β expression induced by nsp1, suggesting that AP-1 is essential for IL-1β production. In addition, we showed that TRAF6 was required for nsp1 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway by interacting with each other. Truncation and deletion mutation analysis indicated that R308 and R375 amino acids were important for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Finally, we constructed the recombinant viruses mutated at R308 and R375 and found that the mutated virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired the ability to induce IL-1β compared to the wild-type strain. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of IL-1β production induced by PRRSV and help us further understand the pathogenesis of PRRSV infection. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) has been prevalent in China since 2006, causing severe pneumonia in pigs. IL-1β is a proinflammatory cytokine secreted by various cells. In this study, we demonstrated that PRRSV protein nsp1 interacted with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway, consequently inducing the expression of IL-1β. Additionally, our findings revealed that R308 and R375 in nsp1 were critical amino acid residues for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Notably, the recombinant virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired ability to induce proinflammatory cytokines in vitro compared to the wild-type strain HP-PRRSV. This study helps us further understand HP-PRRSV pathogenesis and provides a new idea for the development of PRRSV vaccines.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) caused by PRRS virus (PRRSV) is a highly contagious disease threatening the global pig industry, with severe pneumonia as a key symptom. The study was needed because IL-1β is upregulated during PRRSV infection but the underlying mechanism remained unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study explored how PRRSV regulated IL-1β production by focusing on the nonstructural protein 1 (nsp1) of highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV). The research involved molecular and cellular experiments to dissect signaling pathways and protein interactions.
analysis.methods: Overexpression of nsp1 was used to induce IL-1β production, with dose-dependence assessed. Inhibitors of p38 and JNK pathways were applied to evaluate their role in IL-1β expression. AP-1 binding motif deletion in the IL-1β promoter was performed to test its necessity. TRAF6 interaction with nsp1 was analyzed via truncation and deletion mutation assays. Recombinant viruses with mutations at R308 and R375 were constructed to assess replication and cytokine induction.
analysis.main_results: HP-PRRSV nsp1 upregulated IL-1β expression, with overexpression inducing IL-1β in a dose-dependent manner. The addition of p38 and JNK inhibitors reduced IL-1β production induced by nsp1, indicating activation of JNK/p38 signaling pathways. Deletion of the AP-1 binding motif in the IL-1β promoter impaired nsp1-induced IL-1β expression. TRAF6 was required for nsp1 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway through interaction with nsp1. Mutations at R308 and R375 in nsp1 disrupted TRAF6 interaction and IL-1β induction. The recombinant virus PRRSV-R308/375A showed significantly reduced replication and impaired ability to induce proinflammatory cytokines compared to the wild-type strain.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that PRRSV nsp1 interacts with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 signaling pathway, driving IL-1β production. The identification of R308 and R375 as critical residues for TRAF6 interaction and IL-1β induction is novel and provides mechanistic insight into PRRSV pathogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings advance understanding of HP-PRRSV pathogenesis by elucidating a specific molecular mechanism of immune activation. They may inform the development of PRRSV vaccines or therapeutic strategies targeting nsp1-TRAF6 interactions to modulate IL-1β-mediated inflammation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and molecular studies without in vivo validation of the recombinant virus's effects in animals. The study relies on abstract-level data, and the generalizability of these findings to natural infection dynamics remains uncertain. The confidence in the evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) induces IL-1β production, a proinflammatory cytokine upregulated during infection. The research demonstrates that the viral nonstructural protein 1 (nsp1) interacts with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 signaling pathway, driving IL-1β expression. Key findings include the dose-dependent induction of IL-1β by nsp1, the necessity of p38 and JNK pathways, and the critical role of AP-1 in promoter activation. Mutations at R308 and R375 in nsp1 disrupt TRAF6 interaction and IL-1β induction, and a recombinant virus with these mutations exhibits reduced replication and cytokine induction. The study provides mechanistic insight into HP-PRRSV pathogenesis and suggests potential targets for vaccine or therapeutic development.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由PRRS病毒(PRRSV)引起的猪繁殖与呼吸综合征(PRRS)是威胁全球养猪业的一种高度传染性疾病,以重症肺炎为主要症状。这项研究是必要的,因为 IL-1β 在 PRRSV 感染期间上调,但其潜在机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过关注高致病性 PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) 的非结构蛋白 1 (nsp1),探讨了 PRRSV 如何调节 IL-1β 的产生。该研究涉及分子和细胞实验来剖析信号通路和蛋白质相互作用。
elements_zh.methods: nsp1 的过表达用于诱导 IL-1β 产生,并评估剂量依赖性。应用 p38 和 JNK 通路抑制剂来评估它们在 IL-1β 表达中的作用。在IL-1β启动子中进行AP-1结合基序删除以测试其必要性。通过截短和缺失 突变 测定分析 TRAF6 与 nsp1 的相互作用。构建 R308 和 R375 处具有 突变 的重组病毒以评估复制和细胞因子诱导。
elements_zh.main_results: HP-PRRSV nsp1上调IL-1β表达,过度表达以剂量依赖性方式诱导IL-1β。添加 p38 和 JNK 抑制剂可减少 nsp1 诱导的 IL-1β 产生,表明 JNK/p38 信号通路被激活。IL-1β 启动子中 AP-1 结合基序的缺失会损害 nsp1 诱导的 IL-1β 表达。nsp1 需要 TRAF6 通过与 nsp1 相互作用来激活 TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 信号通路。nsp1 中 R308 和 R375 处的 突变 破坏了 TRAF6 相互作用和 IL-1β 诱导。与野生型毒株相比,重组病毒 PRRSV-R308/375A 的复制显着减少,诱导促炎细胞因子的能力受损。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,PRRSV nsp1 与 TRAF6 相互作用,激活 TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 信号通路,驱动 IL-1β 产生。R308 和 R375 作为 TRAF6 相互作用和 IL-1β 诱导的关键残基的鉴定是新颖的,并提供了 PRRSV 发病机制 的机制见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过阐明免疫激活的特定分子机制,促进了对 HP-PRRSV 发病机制 的理解。它们可能为 PRRSV 疫苗 的发展或针对 nsp1-TRAF6 相互作用以调节 IL-1β 介导的炎症的治疗策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外和分子研究,而没有对重组病毒在动物中的作用进行体内验证。该研究依赖于抽象水平的数据,这些发现对自然感染动态的普遍性仍然不确定。由于这些限制,证据的可信度被评估为中等。

A significant symptom of PRRS is severe pneumonia. At present, studies have shown that IL-1β is upregulated by PRRSV infection in vivo and in vitro , while the underlying mechanism remains unknown. Here, we explored how PRRSV regulated IL-1β production. We found that HP-PRRSV nsp1 upregulated the expression of IL-1β. Overexpression of nsp1 induced IL-1β production in a dose-dependent manner. Subsequently, we demonstrated that nsp1 enhanced IL-1β expression by activating JNK/p38 signaling pathways, as the addition of p38 and JNK inhibitors reduced IL-1β production induced by nsp1. Moreover, deleting the AP-1 binding motif in porcine IL-1β promoter impaired IL-1β expression induced by nsp1, suggesting that AP-1 is essential for IL-1β production. In addition, we showed that TRAF6 was required for nsp1 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway by interacting with each other. Truncation and deletion mutation analysis indicated that R308 and R375 amino acids were important for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Finally, we constructed the recombinant viruses mutated at R308 and R375 and found that the mutated virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired the ability to induce IL-1β compared to the wild-type strain. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of IL-1β production induced by PRRSV and help us further understand the pathogenesis of PRRSV infection. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (HP-PRRSV) has been prevalent in China since 2006, causing severe pneumonia in pigs. IL-1β is a proinflammatory cytokine secreted by various cells. In this study, we demonstrated that PRRSV protein nsp1 interacted with TRAF6 to activate the TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 signaling pathway, consequently inducing the expression of IL-1β. Additionally, our findings revealed that R308 and R375 in nsp1 were critical amino acid residues for nsp1 to interact with TRAF6 and induce IL-1β production. Notably, the recombinant virus PRRSV-R308/375A exhibited a significantly reduced replication rate and impaired ability to induce proinflammatory cytokines in vitro compared to the wild-type strain HP-PRRSV. This study helps us further understand HP-PRRSV pathogenesis and provides a new idea for the development of PRRSV vaccines.
abstract_zh: 【摘要】:猪繁殖与呼吸综合征(PRRS)是由PRRS病毒(PRRSV)引起的一种高度传染性疾病,严重威胁全球养猪业。PRRS的一个显着症状是严重肺炎。目前,体内外研究表明PRRSV感染可上调IL-1β,但其具体机​​制尚不清楚。在这里,我们探讨了 PRRSV 如何调节 IL-1β 的产生。我们发现 HP-PRRSV nsp1 上调 IL-1β 的表达。nsp1 的过表达以剂量依赖性方式诱导 IL-1β 产生。随后,我们证明nsp1通过激活JNK/p38信号通路增强IL-1β表达,因为添加p38和JNK抑制剂减少了nsp1诱导的IL-1β产生。此外,删除猪IL-1β启动子中的AP-1结合基序会损害nsp1诱导的IL-1β表达,表明AP-1对于IL-1β的产生至关重要。此外,我们还发现 nsp1 需要 TRAF6 通过相互作用来激活 TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 信号通路。截短和缺失 突变 分析表明 R308 和 R375 氨基酸对于 nsp1 与 TRAF6 相互作用并诱导 IL-1β 产生很重要。最后,我们构建了R308和R375突变的重组病毒,发现突变病毒PRRSV-R308/375A与野生型毒株相比,复制率显着降低,诱导IL-1β的能力受损。这些发现为PRRSV诱导IL-1β产生的分子机制提供了新的见解,并帮助我们进一步了解PRRSV感染的发病机制。重要性 自2006年以来,高致病性猪繁殖与呼吸综合征病毒(HP-PRRSV)在中国流行,导致猪出现严重肺炎。IL-1β是多种细胞分泌的促炎细胞因子。在本研究中,我们证明PRRSV蛋白nsp1与TRAF6相互作用激活TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1信号通路,从而诱导IL-1β的表达。此外,我们的研究结果表明,nsp1 中的 R308 和 R375 是 nsp1 与 TRAF6 相互作用并诱导 IL-1β 产生的关键氨基酸残基。值得注意的是,与野生型菌株 HP-PRRSV 相比,重组病毒 PRRSV-R308/375A 的复制率显着降低,体外诱导促炎细胞因子的能力受损。本研究有助于我们进一步了解HP-PRRSV 发病机制,并为PRRSV 疫苗的开发提供新思路。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 由PRRS病毒(PRRSV)引起的猪繁殖与呼吸综合征(PRRS)是威胁全球养猪业的一种高度传染性疾病,以重症肺炎为主要症状。这项研究是必要的,因为 IL-1β 在 PRRSV 感染期间上调,但其潜在机制仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过关注高致病性 PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) 的非结构蛋白 1 (nsp1),探讨了 PRRSV 如何调节 IL-1β 的产生。该研究涉及分子和细胞实验来剖析信号通路和蛋白质相互作用。
analysis_zh.methods: nsp1 的过表达用于诱导 IL-1β 产生,并评估剂量依赖性。应用 p38 和 JNK 通路抑制剂来评估它们在 IL-1β 表达中的作用。在IL-1β启动子中进行AP-1结合基序删除以测试其必要性。通过截短和缺失 突变 测定分析 TRAF6 与 nsp1 的相互作用。构建 R308 和 R375 处具有 突变 的重组病毒以评估复制和细胞因子诱导。
analysis_zh.main_results: HP-PRRSV nsp1上调IL-1β表达,过度表达以剂量依赖性方式诱导IL-1β。添加 p38 和 JNK 抑制剂可减少 nsp1 诱导的 IL-1β 产生,表明 JNK/p38 信号通路被激活。IL-1β 启动子中 AP-1 结合基序的缺失会损害 nsp1 诱导的 IL-1β 表达。nsp1 需要 TRAF6 通过与 nsp1 相互作用来激活 TAK1/JNK/p38/AP-1 信号通路。nsp1 中 R308 和 R375 处的 突变 破坏了 TRAF6 相互作用和 IL-1β 诱导。与野生型毒株相比,重组病毒 PRRSV-R308/375A 的复制显着减少,诱导促炎细胞因子的能力受损。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,PRRSV nsp1 与 TRAF6 相互作用,激活 TAK1/p38/JNK/AP-1 信号通路,驱动 IL-1β 产生。R308 和 R375 作为 TRAF6 相互作用和 IL-1β 诱导的关键残基的鉴定是新颖的,并提供了 PRRSV 发病机制 的机制见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过阐明免疫激活的特定分子机制,促进了对 HP-PRRSV 发病机制 的理解。它们可能为 PRRSV 疫苗 的发展或针对 nsp1-TRAF6 相互作用以调节 IL-1β 介导的炎症的治疗策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外和分子研究,而没有对重组病毒在动物中的作用进行体内验证。该研究依赖于抽象水平的数据,这些发现对自然感染动态的普遍性仍然不确定。由于这些限制,证据的可信度被评估为中等。

title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections and deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly, while existing antiviral drugs have limited efficacy and safety. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds with antiviral and immunomodulatory activities, may address this unmet need by targeting RSV replication and inflammation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the anti-RSV activity of sophora alkaloids and their liposomal formulations in murine models of RSV infection using intratracheal administration. Sophocarpine (SC), identified as the most effective alkaloid, was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance pulmonary retention and therapeutic effects.
analysis.methods: The study assessed RSV replication and pulmonary inflammation in mice treated with free SC or SC-loaded liposomes via intratracheal administration. Mechanistic investigations focused on the inhibition of ERK1/2 phosphorylation through regulation of the MEK/ERK signaling pathway to suppress viral proliferation and inflammatory responses.
analysis.main_results: In vivo studies showed that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced mortality in RSV-infected mice, and SC-loaded liposomes outperformed free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study clarifies that sophora alkaloids counteract RSV infection by inhibiting ERK1/2 phosphorylation via the MEK/ERK pathway, and demonstrates that liposomal encapsulation of SC enhances its anti-RSV efficacy in vivo, representing a novel formulation strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that liposomal formulations of sophora alkaloids, particularly SC, could improve therapeutic outcomes for RSV infection by enhancing pulmonary drug retention and antiviral activity, potentially addressing limitations of current treatments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to murine models and does not report human clinical data, safety profiles, or comparative efficacy against standard-of-care antivirals, warranting cautious interpretation and further translational research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity of sophora alkaloids and evaluated the enhanced efficacy of sophocarpine (SC) when encapsulated in liposomes via intratracheal administration in murine models. RSV is a major cause of severe lower respiratory infections with limited treatment options, and sophora alkaloids were explored for their antiviral and immunomodulatory properties. Mechanistically, the alkaloids inhibit RSV replication by suppressing ERK1/2 phosphorylation through the MEK/ERK signaling pathway. In vivo, sophora alkaloids reduced mortality in RSV-infected mice, and SC-loaded liposomes outperformed free SC in reducing viral replication and pulmonary inflammation. The study highlights the potential of liposomal formulations to improve therapeutic outcomes for RSV infection, though findings are confined to animal models and lack human safety or efficacy data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)会导致婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和死亡,而现有的抗病毒药物药物的疗效和安全性有限。槐生物碱是具有 抗病毒药物 和免疫调节活性的天然化合物,可以通过针对 RSV 复制和炎症来解决这一未满足的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过气管内给药评估了槐花生物碱及其脂质体制剂在 RSV 感染小鼠模型中的抗 RSV 活性。槐果碱 (SC) 被认为是最有效的生物碱,被封装在脂质体中以增强肺滞留和治疗效果。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究评估了通过气管内施用游离 SC 或装载 SC 的脂质体治疗小鼠的 RSV 复制和肺部炎症。机制研究重点是通过调节 MEK/ERK 信号通路抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化,从而抑制病毒增殖和炎症反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 体内研究表明,槐花生物碱显着降低了 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率,并且负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻小鼠模型中的肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究阐明苦参生物碱通过 MEK/ERK 途径抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化来对抗 RSV 感染,并证明 SC 的脂质体封装增强了其体内抗 RSV 功效,代表了一种新颖的制剂策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,槐花生物碱的脂质体制剂,特别是 SC,可以通过增强肺部药物保留和 抗病毒药物 活性来改善 RSV 感染的治疗结果,从而可能解决当前 治疗 的局限性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于小鼠模型,没有报告人类临床数据、安全性概况或与标准治疗 抗病毒药物 的比较疗效,需要谨慎解释和进一步的转化研究。

analysis_en.main_results: In vivo studies showed that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced mortality in RSV-infected mice, and SC-loaded liposomes outperformed free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study clarifies that sophora alkaloids counteract RSV infection by inhibiting ERK1/2 phosphorylation via the MEK/ERK pathway, and demonstrates that liposomal encapsulation of SC enhances its anti-RSV efficacy in vivo, representing a novel formulation strategy.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that liposomal formulations of sophora alkaloids, particularly SC, could improve therapeutic outcomes for RSV infection by enhancing pulmonary drug retention and antiviral activity, potentially addressing limitations of current treatments.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to murine models and does not report human clinical data, safety profiles, or comparative efficacy against standard-of-care antivirals, warranting cautious interpretation and further translational research.

title_zh: 槐生物碱的抗人呼吸道合胞病毒活性评价及脂质体气管内给药增强功效的评价
source_body_en: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.
abstract_zh: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和相关死亡的主要原因。由于 RSV 的高 突变 发生率以及现有 抗病毒药物 药物的疗效和安全性有限,RSV 的临床管理具有挑战性。苦参生物碱是从苦参中提取的天然化合物,具有广谱 抗病毒药物 和免疫调节活性。从机制上讲,RSV依赖ERK1/2磷酸化来促进病毒复制和传播,而槐花生物碱通过调节MEK/ERK信号通路抑制ERK1/2磷酸化,从而抑制病毒增殖和RSV感染引起的炎症反应。体内研究表明,槐花生物碱通过气管内给药可显着降低 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率。为了进一步增强药物的肺滞留,采用脂质体来提高苦参生物碱的治疗效果。槐果碱(SC)作为抗RSV感染最有效的生物碱,将其封装在脂质体中以增强其抗RSV感染的效果。体内研究表明,在 RSV 感染的小鼠模型中,负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。本研究不仅阐明了苦参生物碱抗RSV感染的机制,而且提供了SC的脂质体制剂以提高抗RSV的治疗效果。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)会导致婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和死亡,而现有的抗病毒药物药物的疗效和安全性有限。槐生物碱是具有 抗病毒药物 和免疫调节活性的天然化合物,可以通过针对 RSV 复制和炎症来解决这一未满足的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过气管内给药评估了槐花生物碱及其脂质体制剂在 RSV 感染小鼠模型中的抗 RSV 活性。槐果碱 (SC) 被认为是最有效的生物碱,被封装在脂质体中以增强肺滞留和治疗效果。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究评估了通过气管内施用游离 SC 或装载 SC 的脂质体治疗小鼠的 RSV 复制和肺部炎症。机制研究重点是通过调节 MEK/ERK 信号通路抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化,从而抑制病毒增殖和炎症反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 体内研究表明,槐花生物碱显着降低了 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率,并且负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻小鼠模型中的肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究阐明苦参生物碱通过 MEK/ERK 途径抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化来对抗 RSV 感染,并证明 SC 的脂质体封装增强了其体内抗 RSV 功效,代表了一种新颖的制剂策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,槐花生物碱的脂质体制剂,特别是 SC,可以通过增强肺部药物保留和 抗病毒药物 活性来改善 RSV 感染的治疗结果,从而可能解决当前 治疗 的局限性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于小鼠模型,没有报告人类临床数据、安全性概况或与标准治疗 抗病毒药物 的比较疗效,需要谨慎解释和进一步的转化研究。

title: Global Research Trends in Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Research: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Background/Objectives: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections and has long posed challenges to vaccine development because of historical safety concerns and the complexity of protective immunity. Recent advances in structural biology, maternal immunization, vaccines for older adults, and monoclonal antibodies have reshaped this field. This study aimed to analyze global research trends in RSV vaccine research using a bibliometric approach. Methods: A bibliometric study was conducted using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on April 1, 2026. Original articles and reviews published between 1968 and 2026 were selected through a title-based search strategy related to RSV and vaccination. Bibliometric indicators, citation patterns, collaboration networks, source distribution, and thematic structures were analyzed using Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny in R. Results: The final sample included 1,455 documents from 394 sources, with an annual growth rate of 8.7%. Scientific production increased markedly after 2010, with stronger acceleration after 2020. The United States led global output, followed by China, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the Netherlands. Vaccine was the most productive and locally influential source. Citation analysis identified the formalin-inactivated RSV vaccine studies from 1969 and the prefusion F protein study from 2013 as major intellectual milestones. Keyword analysis showed a shift from disease burden, epidemiology, and pathogenesis toward immunization, immunogenicity, maternal vaccination, older adults, and monoclonal antibodies. Conclusions: RSV vaccine research has evolved from a historically safety-constrained field to a mature translational area focused on prevention, implementation, real-world effectiveness, and equitable access.
authors: Andréia Rodrigues Moura da Costa Valle

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是急性呼吸道感染的主要原因,并且由于历史安全问题和保护性免疫的复杂性,长期以来对 疫苗 的开发构成挑战。结构生物学、母体免疫、老年人 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的最新进展重塑了这一领域。本研究旨在使用文献计量方法分析 RSV 疫苗 研究的全球研究趋势。方法:使用 2026 年 4 月 1 日从 Web of Science 核心合集中检索的记录进行文献计量研究。通过与 RSV 和 疫苗接种 相关的基于标题的搜索策略选择 1968 年至 2026 年间发表的原创文章和评论。使用 R 中的 Bibliometrix 和 Biblioshiny 分析文献计量指标、引用模式、协作网络、来源分布和主题结构。结果:最终样本包括来自 394 个来源的 1,455 篇文献,年增长率为 8.7%。科学产出在 2010 年之后显着增长,2020 年之后加速加速。美国引领全球产出,其次是中国、英国、加拿大和荷兰。疫苗 是最具生产力和当地影响力的来源。引文分析将 1969 年的福尔马林灭活 RSV 疫苗 研究和 2013 年的预融合 F 蛋白研究确定为主要的智力里程碑。关键词分析显示,从疾病负担、流行病学 和 发病机制 转向免疫、免疫原性、母体 疫苗接种、老年人和单克隆抗体。结论:RSV 疫苗 研究已从历史上安全受限的领域发展成为专注于预防、实施、现实世界有效性和公平获取的成熟转化领域。

title: Disparities in Nirsevimab Uptake Over 2 Seasons
abstract: Nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis, debuted during the 2023 to 2024 RSV season. Despite universal recommendation, both incomplete uptake and disparities in nirsevimab receipt exist.1,2 Nirsevimab administration is important because it is highly effective in preventing RSV infection and hospitalization in young infants.3 The objective of this study was to determine if (1) nirsevimab uptake increased within a large pediatric primary care network and (2) if previously identified disparities persisted in its second RSV season.A cohort of infants younger than 8 months from 32 primary care practices across New Jersey and Pennsylvania within the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia network was generated as previously described.1 Infants with maternal RSV vaccination were excluded. The 2023 to 2024 RSV season was defined as October 1, 2023, through March 31, 2024, and the 2024 to 2025 RSV season as October 1, 2024, through March 31, 2025. We included infants ineligible to receive nirsevimab in the birth hospital due to being born outside of RSV season (April through September) and, therefore, reliant on their primary care practice to receive it, allowing the exploration of factors potentially associated with nirsevimab uptake within the context of the patient’s medical home.Nirsevimab administration and patient age, sex, race and ethnicity, birthweight, insurance status, Childhood Opportunity Index (COI), and visit type were extracted from the electronic health record (EHR).4,5 Race and ethnicity data were self-reported by patients in the EHR. Although race is a social construct, it is included in the analyses because differences in nirsevimab receipt can highlight potential inequities. Vaccine adherence analyses (up to date for Haemophilus influenzae type b, poliovirus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis by age 9 months) were conducted as previously described.1Descriptive comparisons of uptake across subgroups are presented as unadjusted proportions. Logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with nirsevimab receipt during each season. We fit a pooled logistic regression model including covariates and season-by-covariate interaction terms. Adjusted ORs and 95% CIs were estimated, and interaction terms were used. Inverse probability weighting was used to address missing data.The eligible primary care cohort included 13 897 patients across both seasons (Supplement Figure 1). Comparable with the 2023 to 2024 season, patients in the 2024 to 2025 season were majority male (51.7%), White (53.0%), non-Hispanic/Latino (81.7%), and nonpublicly insured (64.8%) (Table 1). Preterm birth was not included in Figure 1 as prematurity was colinear with low birthweight as described in our previous work. Although nirsevimab uptake increased from 35% in the 2023 to 2024 season to 67% in the 2024 to 2025 season, lower rates of nirsevimab administration to infants with public insurance (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.50–0.67 compared with private insurance), of Black race (OR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56–0.82 compared with White infants), and at an older age at start of RSV season (OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79–0.84 for each additional month) persisted into season 2 (Figure 1). Lower COI no longer remained significant (OR, 0.90; 95% CI 0.71–1.14).Overall, 23.5% of children received nirsevimab at nurse (vaccine administration only) visits. Notably, infants of White race (30.9%), with very high COI (32.9%), and with nonpublic insurance (31.1%) had higher unadjusted rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits compared with those of Black race (7.1%), with public insurance (8.4%), and with low COI (6.4%). Infants who were fully vaccinated (38.7%–75.5%), partially vaccinated (21.7%–43.3%), and unvaccinated (0.7%–2.4%) against other routine pathogens all increased nirsevimab uptake from the 2023–2024 to 2024–2025 RSV season.Although primary care nirsevimab uptake doubled between the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 RSV season, the majority of previously identified disparities in RSV administration remained across this large, diverse primary care network. These data suggest that targeted interventions are required to increase protection for all infants at risk of RSV infection.Infants who were publicly insured or Black remained significantly less likely to receive nirsevimab. The reasons for the observed disparities are unclear. Stark differences in rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits—encounters scheduled outside of normal well and sick visits and specifically created for vaccine administration—suggest health care access might contribute. Future work could explore interventions to increase nirsevimab uptake by expanding access to nurse visits and encouraging uptake during sick visits for infants with mild illnesses. Additional factors including institutional racism and differences in trust in vaccine safety among sociodemographic strata may also contribute but were not explored in the current study.Unsurprisingly, nirsevimab uptake was highest among those fully vaccinated with routine immunizations, which has been shown with other respiratory vaccines.6 Although all groups increased uptake from the 2023–2024 season to the 2024–2025 season, universally unvaccinated children almost never received nirsevimab.Limitations include the single-center study design, which limits generalizability, and inability to identify reasons for lack of nirsevimab administration, which would help guide quality improvement efforts. Although other studies confirm these disparities, to our knowledge, this is the first to demonstrate that disparities persist across multiple seasons despite increased uptake and demands examination of the drivers of these disparities to inform efforts to increase nirsevimab administration for all eligible infants.7–9

Overall uptake increased from 35% in 2023–2024 to 67% in 2024–2025, yet disparities persisted: infants with public insurance and of Black race were significantly less likely to receive nirsevimab, and older age at season start was associated with lower receipt.
