title_zh: Disparities in Nirsevimab Uptake Over 2 Seasons
source_body_en: Nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis, debuted during the 2023 to 2024 RSV season. Despite universal recommendation, both incomplete uptake and disparities in nirsevimab receipt exist.1,2 Nirsevimab administration is important because it is highly effective in preventing RSV infection and hospitalization in young infants.3 The objective of this study was to determine if (1) nirsevimab uptake increased within a large pediatric primary care network and (2) if previously identified disparities persisted in its second RSV season.A cohort of infants younger than 8 months from 32 primary care practices across New Jersey and Pennsylvania within the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia network was generated as previously described.1 Infants with maternal RSV vaccination were excluded. The 2023 to 2024 RSV season was defined as October 1, 2023, through March 31, 2024, and the 2024 to 2025 RSV season as October 1, 2024, through March 31, 2025. We included infants ineligible to receive nirsevimab in the birth hospital due to being born outside of RSV season (April through September) and, therefore, reliant on their primary care practice to receive it, allowing the exploration of factors potentially associated with nirsevimab uptake within the context of the patient’s medical home.Nirsevimab administration and patient age, sex, race and ethnicity, birthweight, insurance status, Childhood Opportunity Index (COI), and visit type were extracted from the electronic health record (EHR).4,5 Race and ethnicity data were self-reported by patients in the EHR. Although race is a social construct, it is included in the analyses because differences in nirsevimab receipt can highlight potential inequities. Vaccine adherence analyses (up to date for Haemophilus influenzae type b, poliovirus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis by age 9 months) were conducted as previously described.1Descriptive comparisons of uptake across subgroups are presented as unadjusted proportions. Logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with nirsevimab receipt during each season. We fit a pooled logistic regression model including covariates and season-by-covariate interaction terms. Adjusted ORs and 95% CIs were estimated, and interaction terms were used. Inverse probability weighting was used to address missing data.The eligible primary care cohort included 13 897 patients across both seasons (Supplement Figure 1). Comparable with the 2023 to 2024 season, patients in the 2024 to 2025 season were majority male (51.7%), White (53.0%), non-Hispanic/Latino (81.7%), and nonpublicly insured (64.8%) (Table 1). Preterm birth was not included in Figure 1 as prematurity was colinear with low birthweight as described in our previous work. Although nirsevimab uptake increased from 35% in the 2023 to 2024 season to 67% in the 2024 to 2025 season, lower rates of nirsevimab administration to infants with public insurance (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.50–0.67 compared with private insurance), of Black race (OR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56–0.82 compared with White infants), and at an older age at start of RSV season (OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79–0.84 for each additional month) persisted into season 2 (Figure 1). Lower COI no longer remained significant (OR, 0.90; 95% CI 0.71–1.14).Overall, 23.5% of children received nirsevimab at nurse (vaccine administration only) visits. Notably, infants of White race (30.9%), with very high COI (32.9%), and with nonpublic insurance (31.1%) had higher unadjusted rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits compared with those of Black race (7.1%), with public insurance (8.4%), and with low COI (6.4%). Infants who were fully vaccinated (38.7%–75.5%), partially vaccinated (21.7%–43.3%), and unvaccinated (0.7%–2.4%) against other routine pathogens all increased nirsevimab uptake from the 2023–2024 to 2024–2025 RSV season.Although primary care nirsevimab uptake doubled between the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 RSV season, the majority of previously identified disparities in RSV administration remained across this large, diverse primary care network. These data suggest that targeted interventions are required to increase protection for all infants at risk of RSV infection.Infants who were publicly insured or Black remained significantly less likely to receive nirsevimab. The reasons for the observed disparities are unclear. Stark differences in rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits—encounters scheduled outside of normal well and sick visits and specifically created for vaccine administration—suggest health care access might contribute. Future work could explore interventions to increase nirsevimab uptake by expanding access to nurse visits and encouraging uptake during sick visits for infants with mild illnesses. Additional factors including institutional racism and differences in trust in vaccine safety among sociodemographic strata may also contribute but were not explored in the current study.Unsurprisingly, nirsevimab uptake was highest among those fully vaccinated with routine immunizations, which has been shown with other respiratory vaccines.6 Although all groups increased uptake from the 2023–2024 season to the 2024–2025 season, universally unvaccinated children almost never received nirsevimab.Limitations include the single-center study design, which limits generalizability, and inability to identify reasons for lack of nirsevimab administration, which would help guide quality improvement efforts. Although other studies confirm these disparities, to our knowledge, this is the first to demonstrate that disparities persist across multiple seasons despite increased uptake and demands examination of the drivers of these disparities to inform efforts to increase nirsevimab administration for all eligible infants.7–9

title: RSV can infect the human nasal epithelium via the basolateral route and shows distinct subgroup infectivity and basal cell tropism
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes millions of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised populations every year. RSV infection initiates in the upper respiratory tract and can progress to the lower airways, resulting in bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and even death. RSV primarily infects epithelial cells apically, but we hypothesized that basolateral exposure of the respiratory epithelium could provide an alternative mechanism of infection that contributes to LRTI development. Using a human nose organoid-air-liquid interface (HNO-ALI) model, we performed apical and basolateral inoculations with contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario [RSV/A/ON] and RSV/B/Buenos Aires [RSV/B/BA]) representing the two RSV subgroups (A and B) in both adult- and infant-derived HNO-ALIs. Basolateral RSV exposure resulted in delayed viral replication and apical release compared to apical infection. A statistically significant difference in basolateral infection frequency was observed between RSV/B/BA and RSV/A/ON (81.3% versus 25%). Basolateral infection selectively targeted a rare basal cell population, while preserving epithelial integrity. Using undifferentiated HNO-ALIs, we determined for the first time that Krt23+ activated basal cells are uniquely susceptible to RSV infection, a finding we confirmed in fully differentiated HNO-ALIs. Together, our findings show that RSV can infect the respiratory epithelium from the basolateral side by initially targeting a rare subset of basal cells before spreading apically to ciliated cells. Moreover, RSV/B/BA may have an advantage over RSV/A/ON in utilizing the basolateral infection route. These findings highlight an alternative RSV infection pathway and could be a potential mechanism for RSV spread to the lower airways. IMPORTANCE Understanding the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is essential to understanding and preventing acute and long-term sequelae from infection. The canonical understanding of RSV infection is that the virus infects and is restricted to the apical ciliated cells upon inhalation or fomite exposure. We demonstrate that an alternative route of infection—the basolateral route—can be utilized by RSV to infect the apical ciliated cells of the respiratory epithelium. We also show for the first time a novel difference in infectivity between the two contemporaneous RSV strains (RSV/A/Ontario and RSV/B/Buenos Aires). In addition, we describe a rare basal subset—the Krt23+ activated basal cells—that are uniquely susceptible to RSV, expanding the known cellular tropism of RSV. Infection of basal cells can impact airway differentiation, homeostasis, and remodeling. Overall, our findings expand on RSV pathogenesis and indicate there are alternative mechanisms of infection and cell populations that are susceptible to RSV.

full_text: Abstract Introduction: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in infants and young children. This study evaluated clinical and laboratory factors associated with prolonged hospitalization in pediatric RSV infection. Methods: This retrospective study included children under 18 years of age hospitalized with LRTI and confirmed RSV infection at our center between 2023 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected from hospital records. Patients were divided into two groups according to length of stay (LOS): ≤2 days and >2 days. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed using the backward stepwise method. Results: A total of 185 RSV-infected children were analyzed. The median age was 2 months, and 51.9% were male. Patients with LOS >2 days had significantly higher rates of PICU admission, non-invasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, and secondary bacterial infections. Laboratory findings showed higher lymphocyte counts and BUN levels in the prolonged-stay group, whereas MPV levels were lower. No mortality was observed. In the multivariate logistic regression analysis, PICU stay was associated with approximately 12-fold increased risk of hospitalization longer than 2 days. Conclusion: Hospitalization longer than 2 days was associated with a more severe clinical course. In the multivariate logistic regression analysis, PICU stay was the main factor associated with hospitalization longer than 2 days. Lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN may provide supportive clinical information; however, their independent prognostic value remains uncertain.

title_original: Predictors of Prolonged Hospitalization in Pediatric Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children, yet predictors of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors associated with hospitalization exceeding 2 days in pediatric RSV infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study enrolled children under 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV lower respiratory tract infection at a single center between 2023 and 2025. Patients were stratified by length of stay (≤2 days vs >2 days) for comparative analysis.
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were abstracted from hospital records. Multivariate logistic regression with backward stepwise selection was used to identify predictors of prolonged hospitalization (>2 days).
analysis.main_results: Among 185 RSV-infected children, the median age was 2 months and 51.9% were male. Patients with prolonged hospitalization (>2 days) had higher rates of PICU admission, non-invasive ventilation, mechanical ventilation, and secondary bacterial infections. Laboratory findings showed higher lymphocyte counts and BUN levels, while MPV levels were lower in the prolonged-stay group. No mortality occurred.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret prolonged hospitalization as reflecting a more severe clinical course in pediatric RSV infection. They highlight PICU stay as the dominant predictor of extended hospitalization and suggest that lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN may offer supportive prognostic information, though their independent value remains uncertain.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform risk stratification and resource allocation for pediatric RSV hospitalizations by identifying patients at risk of prolonged stays. The identified associations could guide clinical monitoring and early intervention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center retrospective design and absence of external validation limit generalizability and causal inference. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to potential unmeasured confounding and the uncertain independent prognostic value of laboratory markers.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 185 children hospitalized with RSV lower respiratory tract infection between 2023 and 2025 identified factors associated with prolonged hospitalization (>2 days). Patients with extended stays had higher rates of intensive care, ventilatory support, and secondary bacterial infections, alongside elevated lymphocyte counts and BUN, and lower MPV. Multivariate analysis indicated that PICU stay was associated with a 12-fold increased risk of prolonged hospitalization, while lymphocyte count, MPV, and BUN showed supportive but uncertain prognostic value. The study suggests that clinical severity markers may aid risk stratification, though single-center design and retrospective data limit generalizability and causal conclusions.

title: Changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia in Changzhou, China, 2018-2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a significant cause of hospitalization and mortality in children. Non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic were associated with changes in the transmission dynamics of respiratory pathogens. The present study aimed to analyze changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with CAP in a single-center pediatric cohort in Changzhou, China, before and after the outbreak of COVID-19. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed demographic information, hospitalization records, and pathogen-detection results of children admitted for CAP at Changzhou Children's Hospital, Jiangsu Province, China, from 2018 to 2023. The analyzed pathogens included eight target bacteria and seven respiratory viruses. RESULTS: A total of 29,552 children hospitalized with CAP were included, including 15,124 in the pre-pandemic period, 9024 in the pandemic period, and 5404 in the post-pandemic period. The male-to-female ratio was 1.42:1, and the median age was 16 months (IQR: 5.0-37.0). Hospitalizations generally peaked in autumn and winter from 2018 to 2022, whereas an off-season peak occurred in May 2023. The overall bacterial positivity increased from 9.94% before the pandemic to 13.96% during the pandemic and 13.68% after the pandemic, while viral positivity increased from 16.52% to 21.43% and 21.06%, respectively. In contrast, coinfection positivity decreased from 6.89% before the pandemic to 5.13% during the pandemic and 3.02% after the pandemic. Across all three periods, Escherichia coli consistently ranked first among bacterial detections, while RSV remained the predominant virus among viral detections. CONCLUSIONS: Noticeable shifts in the detection spectrum and positivity rates of common bacterial and viral pathogens were observed among hospitalized children with CAP following the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 prevention and control policies. Continuous long-term surveillance is needed to refine targeted prevention strategies and optimize clinical treatment protocols for pediatric CAP. CLINICAL TRIAL: Not applicable.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Changzhou, China, from 2018 to 2023, focusing on the impact of non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic on pathogen detection patterns and transmission dynamics in pediatric CAP.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a retrospective single-center study analyzing demographic information, hospitalization records, and pathogen-detection results of 29,552 children admitted for CAP at Changzhou Children's Hospital, including 15,124 in the pre-pandemic period, 9,024 during the pandemic, and 5,404 in the post-pandemic period. The study reviewed eight target bacteria and seven respiratory viruses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review reports a consistent increase in bacterial and viral positivity rates among hospitalized children with CAP across the three periods: bacterial positivity rose from 9.94% pre-pandemic to 13.96% during the pandemic and 13.68% post-pandemic, while viral positivity increased from 16.52% to 21.43% and 21.06%, respectively. Coinfection positivity decreased from 6.89% pre-pandemic to 5.13% during the pandemic and 3.02% post-pandemic. Escherichia coli and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remained the most frequently detected bacterial and viral pathogens, respectively.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific mechanisms underlying the observed shifts in pathogen detection patterns or the long-term clinical implications of these changes. Additionally, the single-center design and retrospective nature limit generalizability, and the study does not address potential confounding factors such as vaccination coverage or local policy variations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for continuous long-term surveillance to refine targeted prevention strategies and optimize clinical treatment protocols for pediatric CAP, particularly in light of the observed shifts in pathogen detection patterns following the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 prevention and control policies.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes changes in the pathogenic characteristics of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Changzhou, China, from 2018 to 2023, focusing on the impact of non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Using retrospective data from 29,552 pediatric CAP hospitalizations, the study found consistent increases in bacterial and viral positivity rates across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods, alongside a decline in coinfection rates. Escherichia coli and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remained the most frequently detected pathogens. The review underscores the need for ongoing surveillance to adapt prevention and treatment strategies for pediatric CAP in response to evolving pathogen dynamics.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 2018 年至 2023 年中国常州社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 住院儿童病原学特征的变化,重点关注 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后非药物干预 (NPI) 对儿科 CAP 病原检测模式和 传播 动态的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价是一项回顾性单中心研究,分析了常州儿童医院收治的 29,552 名 CAP 儿童的人口统计信息、住院记录和病原体检测结果,其中疫情前 15,124 名,疫情期间 9,024 名,疫情后 5,404 名。该研究回顾了八种目标细菌和七种呼吸道病毒。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述报告说,三个时期内CAP住院儿童的细菌和病毒阳性率持续上升:细菌阳性率从大流行前的9.94%上升到大流行期间的13.96%和大流行后的13.68%,而病毒阳性率分别从16.52%上升到21.43%和21.06%。混合感染阳性率从大流行前的 6.89% 下降至大流行期间的 5.13% 和大流行后的 3.02%。大肠杆菌和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然分别是最常检测到的细菌和病毒病原体。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告观察到的病原体检测模式变化的具体机制或这些变化的长期临床影响。此外,单中心设计和回顾性限制了普遍性,并且该研究没有解决潜在的混杂因素,例如 疫苗接种 覆盖范围或当地政策变化。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要持续长期的 监测 来完善有针对性的预防策略并优化儿科 CAP 的临床 治疗 方案,特别是考虑到在实施和放松 COVID-19 预防和控制政策后观察到的病原体检测模式的变化。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 2018 年至 2023 年中国常州社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 住院儿童病原学特征的变化,重点关注 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后非药物干预 (NPI) 对儿科 CAP 病原检测模式和 传播 动态的影响。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价是一项回顾性单中心研究,分析了常州儿童医院收治的 29,552 名 CAP 儿童的人口统计信息、住院记录和病原体检测结果,其中疫情前 15,124 名,疫情期间 9,024 名,疫情后 5,404 名。该研究回顾了八种目标细菌和七种呼吸道病毒。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述报告说,三个时期内CAP住院儿童的细菌和病毒阳性率持续上升:细菌阳性率从大流行前的9.94%上升到大流行期间的13.96%和大流行后的13.68%,而病毒阳性率分别从16.52%上升到21.43%和21.06%。混合感染阳性率从大流行前的 6.89% 下降至大流行期间的 5.13% 和大流行后的 3.02%。大肠杆菌和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然分别是最常检测到的细菌和病毒病原体。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告观察到的病原体检测模式变化的具体机制或这些变化的长期临床影响。此外,单中心设计和回顾性限制了普遍性,并且该研究没有解决潜在的混杂因素,例如 疫苗接种 覆盖范围或当地政策变化。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要持续长期的 监测 来完善有针对性的预防策略并优化儿科 CAP 的临床 治疗 方案,特别是考虑到在实施和放松 COVID-19 预防和控制政策后观察到的病原体检测模式的变化。

title: Global Viral Lower Respiratory Disease Episodes, Hospitalisations, and Clinical Outcomes by Aetiology, 2010-2021.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) is a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, but pathogen-specific estimates remain limited. We aimed to quantify the global burden of viral LRTD episodes, hospitalisations, and severe clinical outcomes by aetiology from 2010 to 2021. METHODS: We used the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 modelling framework to generate estimates of viral LRTD incidence, hospitalisations, and clinical outcomes from 2010 to 2021 for 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions. Aetiology-specific estimates were generated for five viral categories: influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), SARS-CoV-2, and "other" viral pathogens. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration. Viral LRTD incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool for disease incidence. We then applied location-specific admission scalars, adjusted for healthcare access, to derive hospitalisations. Aetiology-specific clinical outcome proportions-including intensive care unit (ICU) need, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) need, and in-hospital mortality-were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models. These were then applied to the hospitalisation estimates. COVID-19 incidence and hospitalisations were estimated using established GBD COVID-19 methods. All estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). RESULTS: Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4-88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8-101.2) in 2019, while episode rates remained relatively stable at approximately 1200 per 100,000 population. Over the same period, hospitalisation rates increased by 40%, from 103.7 (96.1-111.4) to 145.4 (134.6-156.4) per 100,000 population. In 2020 and 2021, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 resulted in sharp increases in burden, with episodes exceeding 1.1 billion in 2020 and 1.5 billion in 2021. During this period, 2020-2021, episode and hospitalisation rates associated with influenza, RSV, and hMPV declined by nearly 50%. Between 2010 and 2019, global rates of ICU need increased from 16.1 (14.3-18.0) to 23.7 (21.0-26.6) per 100,000 population, IMV need from 7.5 (6.7-8.4) to 11.2 (10.0-12.6), and in-hospital mortality from 9.4 (8.4-10.5) to 13.9 (12.3-15.6). In 2020-2021, SARS-CoV-2 dominated severe outcomes, with in-hospital mortality reaching 87.7 (83.3-92.2) per 100,000 population in 2021. Across the study period, older adults consistently experienced the highest rates of severe outcomes, and substantial regional variation was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Before 2020, global incidence of viral LRTD was stable; however, hospitalisations and severe outcomes increased substantially, suggesting rising clinical severity and healthcare demand. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the global viral LRTD landscape, driving unprecedented increases in hospitalisations, intensive care use, and mortality, while suppressing other respiratory viruses in the years 2020 and 2021. These findings demonstrate a substantial burden of severe viral LRTD globally, with marked age and regional variations, underscoring the importance of sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, adequate healthcare capacity, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) is a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, yet pathogen-specific burden estimates remain insufficient to guide policy and practice. The study addressed the knowledge gap by quantifying the global burden of viral LRTD episodes, hospitalisations, and severe clinical outcomes by aetiology from 2010 to 2021.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a global modelling study using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 framework to estimate viral LRTD burden across 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions from 2010 to 2021. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration.
analysis.methods: Incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool, and hospitalisations were derived using location-specific admission scalars adjusted for healthcare access. Aetiology-specific clinical outcomes—including ICU need, invasive mechanical ventilation need, and in-hospital mortality—were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models and applied to hospitalisation estimates.
analysis.main_results: Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4–88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8–101.2) in 2019, with stable episode rates (~1200 per 100,000). Hospitalisation rates rose by 40% from 103.7 (96.1–111.4) to 145.4 (134.6–156.4) per 100,000 between 2010 and 2019. In 2020–2021, SARS-CoV-2 drove episodes to >1.1 billion (2020) and >1.5 billion (2021), while influenza, RSV, and hMPV episodes declined by nearly 50%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the pre-2020 stability in episode rates alongside rising hospitalisations and severe outcomes as evidence of increasing clinical severity and healthcare demand. The novelty lies in the first comprehensive, aetiology-specific quantification of global viral LRTD burden over 12 years, including the pandemic-era disruption of other respiratory viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform surveillance priorities, healthcare capacity planning, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions by highlighting substantial age- and region-specific variations in severe viral LRTD outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on GBD modelling and input data quality limits precision, particularly for under-resourced regions and less-characterised pathogens. Despite this, the use of established Bayesian meta-regression tools and comprehensive data sources supports a moderate-to-high confidence in the overall burden estimates.

analysis.summary_en: This study quantified the global burden of viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) by aetiology from 2010 to 2021 using the GBD 2021 framework. Before 2020, viral LRTD episode rates were stable (~1200 per 100,000), but hospitalisations and severe outcomes rose by 40% and 46–48%, respectively. The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically altered the landscape, with SARS-CoV-2 driving episodes to over 1.5 billion in 2021 and suppressing other respiratory viruses by nearly 50%. Older adults consistently experienced the highest rates of severe outcomes, and substantial regional variation was observed. The findings underscore the need for sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, healthcare capacity planning, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 病毒性下呼吸道疾病(LRTD)是全球发病率和 死亡率 的主要原因,但病原体特异性负担估计仍不足以指导政策和实践。该研究通过量化 2010 年至 2021 年病毒性 LRTD 发作、住院治疗和严重临床结果(按病因)的全球负担,解决了知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项全球模型研究,使用全球疾病负担 (GBD) 2021 框架来估计 2010 年至 2021 年 204 个国家和地区、21 个地区和 7 个超级区域的病毒 LRTD 负担。数据输入包括 监测 系统、临床信息学、已发表的文献、调查和人口动态登记。
elements_zh.methods: 发病率 使用 DisMod-MR 2.1(一种 GBD 贝叶斯元回归工具)进行估计,并使用根据医疗保健可及性进行调整的特定地点入院标量得出住院情况。使用元回归贝叶斯正则化修剪模型来估计特定病因的临床结果(包括 ICU 需求、有创机械通气需求和住院 死亡率),并将其应用于住院估计。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 2020 年前发病率的稳定以及住院人数和严重后果的增加解释为临床严重程度和医疗保健需求增加的证据。新颖之处在于首次对 12 年来全球病毒 LRTD 负担进行全面、特定病因的量化,包括大流行时期对其他呼吸道病毒的破坏。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过强调严重病毒 LRTD 结果的显着年龄和地区特定差异,为 监测 优先事项、医疗保健能力规划以及公平获得预防和治疗干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究对 GBD 建模和输入数据质量的依赖限制了精度,特别是对于资源贫乏地区和特征较少的病原体。尽管如此,使用已建立的贝叶斯元回归工具和综合数据源支持对总体负担估计的中等到高置信度。

title_zh: 2010-2021 年全球病毒性下呼吸道疾病发病情况、住院情况和按病因划分的临床结果。
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) is a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, but pathogen-specific estimates remain limited. We aimed to quantify the global burden of viral LRTD episodes, hospitalisations, and severe clinical outcomes by aetiology from 2010 to 2021. METHODS: We used the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 modelling framework to generate estimates of viral LRTD incidence, hospitalisations, and clinical outcomes from 2010 to 2021 for 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions. Aetiology-specific estimates were generated for five viral categories: influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), SARS-CoV-2, and "other" viral pathogens. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration. Viral LRTD incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool for disease incidence. We then applied location-specific admission scalars, adjusted for healthcare access, to derive hospitalisations. Aetiology-specific clinical outcome proportions-including intensive care unit (ICU) need, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) need, and in-hospital mortality-were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models. These were then applied to the hospitalisation estimates. COVID-19 incidence and hospitalisations were estimated using established GBD COVID-19 methods. All estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). RESULTS: Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4-88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8-101.2) in 2019, while episode rates remained relatively stable at approximately 1200 per 100,000 population. Over the same period, hospitalisation rates increased by 40%, from 103.7 (96.1-111.4) to 145.4 (134.6-156.4) per 100,000 population. In 2020 and 2021, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 resulted in sharp increases in burden, with episodes exceeding 1.1 billion in 2020 and 1.5 billion in 2021. During this period, 2020-2021, episode and hospitalisation rates associated with influenza, RSV, and hMPV declined by nearly 50%. Between 2010 and 2019, global rates of ICU need increased from 16.1 (14.3-18.0) to 23.7 (21.0-26.6) per 100,000 population, IMV need from 7.5 (6.7-8.4) to 11.2 (10.0-12.6), and in-hospital mortality from 9.4 (8.4-10.5) to 13.9 (12.3-15.6). In 2020-2021, SARS-CoV-2 dominated severe outcomes, with in-hospital mortality reaching 87.7 (83.3-92.2) per 100,000 population in 2021. Across the study period, older adults consistently experienced the highest rates of severe outcomes, and substantial regional variation was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Before 2020, global incidence of viral LRTD was stable; however, hospitalisations and severe outcomes increased substantially, suggesting rising clinical severity and healthcare demand. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the global viral LRTD landscape, driving unprecedented increases in hospitalisations, intensive care use, and mortality, while suppressing other respiratory viruses in the years 2020 and 2021. These findings demonstrate a substantial burden of severe viral LRTD globally, with marked age and regional variations, underscoring the importance of sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, adequate healthcare capacity, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 病毒性下呼吸道疾病(LRTD)是全球发病率和 死亡率 的主要原因,但病原体特异性负担估计仍不足以指导政策和实践。该研究通过量化 2010 年至 2021 年病毒性 LRTD 发作、住院治疗和严重临床结果(按病因)的全球负担,解决了知识差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项全球模型研究,使用全球疾病负担 (GBD) 2021 框架来估计 2010 年至 2021 年 204 个国家和地区、21 个地区和 7 个超级区域的病毒 LRTD 负担。数据输入包括 监测 系统、临床信息学、已发表的文献、调查和人口动态登记。
analysis_zh.methods: 发病率 使用 DisMod-MR 2.1(一种 GBD 贝叶斯元回归工具)进行估计,并使用根据医疗保健可及性进行调整的特定地点入院标量得出住院情况。使用元回归贝叶斯正则化修剪模型来估计特定病因的临床结果(包括 ICU 需求、有创机械通气需求和住院 死亡率),并将其应用于住院估计。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 2020 年前发病率的稳定以及住院人数和严重后果的增加解释为临床严重程度和医疗保健需求增加的证据。新颖之处在于首次对 12 年来全球病毒 LRTD 负担进行全面、特定病因的量化,包括大流行时期对其他呼吸道病毒的破坏。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现通过强调严重病毒 LRTD 结果的显着年龄和地区特定差异,为 监测 优先事项、医疗保健能力规划以及公平获得预防和治疗干预措施提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究对 GBD 建模和输入数据质量的依赖限制了精度,特别是对于资源贫乏地区和特征较少的病原体。尽管如此,使用已建立的贝叶斯元回归工具和综合数据源支持对总体负担估计的中等到高置信度。

title: How Pandemics Have Reshaped the Respiratory Virus Data Landscape in Europe: Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections caused by influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 remain a major public health challenge in Europe. Although surveillance systems for these pathogens are well established, the past 2 decades have seen a rapid diversification of data streams supporting surveillance and research. This expanding data landscape, combined with fragmentation across institutions, sectors, and countries, may limit timely evidence synthesis and effective public health decision-making. Objective This scoping review aimed to identify and characterize data sources used for surveillance and research on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Europe over the past 20 years, and to examine their evolution over time, their alignment with research objectives, and geographic variation in data availability and use. Methods We conducted a scoping review using an objective-driven analytical framework. Empirical reports published between January 2005 and September 2025 were identified in MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Embase. Eligible reports focused on influenza, RSV, or SARS-CoV-2 and included data from 12 European countries. Clinical and interventional studies were excluded. Reports were classified according to 4 research objectives: epidemiological monitoring, evaluation of interventions, assessment of disease burden and health outcomes, and analyses of population adherence and trust toward public health measures. Data sources were grouped into 9 categories, including surveillance systems, electronic health records (EHRs), registries, claims, surveys, digital, environmental, integrated datasets, and others. Results A total of 2564 empirical reports were included. Over time, respiratory virus research relied on an increasingly diverse set of data streams. While surveillance systems remained central, particularly for epidemiological monitoring, their relative dominance declined. From 2020 onward, there was a marked expansion in the use of EHRs, registries, claims data, digital sources, and linked or integrated datasets, alongside increased use of open-access data. Data source use varied by research objective: surveillance data predominated in monitoring and intervention evaluation; EHRs in studies of risk factors and treatment effectiveness; surveys in seroprevalence and public trust analyses; and claims data in assessments of economic burden. Substantial geographic disparities were observed. Northern European countries more frequently used linked and multisource datasets, whereas Southern Europe relied more often on open-access or single-source data. Conclusions This scoping review provides a multipathogen, cross-country mapping of data sources for respiratory virus surveillance and research in Europe over 2 decades, applying an innovative objective-driven framework. Unlike prior reviews focused on single pathogens or data types, it offers a consolidated, comparative perspective based on 2564 reports to inform public health decision-making. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated innovation in data generation and access, but progress remained largely centered on SARS-CoV-2, while structural fragmentation continues to limit timely, integrated data across Europe. Strengthening preparedness will require interoperable infrastructures, federated analysis platforms, sustainable funding for surveillance innovations, and cross-sectoral data sharing.

title_zh: 大流行如何重塑欧洲呼吸道病毒数据格局:范围界定审查
source_body_en: Abstract Background Acute respiratory infections caused by influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 remain a major public health challenge in Europe. Although surveillance systems for these pathogens are well established, the past 2 decades have seen a rapid diversification of data streams supporting surveillance and research. This expanding data landscape, combined with fragmentation across institutions, sectors, and countries, may limit timely evidence synthesis and effective public health decision-making. Objective This scoping review aimed to identify and characterize data sources used for surveillance and research on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Europe over the past 20 years, and to examine their evolution over time, their alignment with research objectives, and geographic variation in data availability and use. Methods We conducted a scoping review using an objective-driven analytical framework. Empirical reports published between January 2005 and September 2025 were identified in MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Embase. Eligible reports focused on influenza, RSV, or SARS-CoV-2 and included data from 12 European countries. Clinical and interventional studies were excluded. Reports were classified according to 4 research objectives: epidemiological monitoring, evaluation of interventions, assessment of disease burden and health outcomes, and analyses of population adherence and trust toward public health measures. Data sources were grouped into 9 categories, including surveillance systems, electronic health records (EHRs), registries, claims, surveys, digital, environmental, integrated datasets, and others. Results A total of 2564 empirical reports were included. Over time, respiratory virus research relied on an increasingly diverse set of data streams. While surveillance systems remained central, particularly for epidemiological monitoring, their relative dominance declined. From 2020 onward, there was a marked expansion in the use of EHRs, registries, claims data, digital sources, and linked or integrated datasets, alongside increased use of open-access data. Data source use varied by research objective: surveillance data predominated in monitoring and intervention evaluation; EHRs in studies of risk factors and treatment effectiveness; surveys in seroprevalence and public trust analyses; and claims data in assessments of economic burden. Substantial geographic disparities were observed. Northern European countries more frequently used linked and multisource datasets, whereas Southern Europe relied more often on open-access or single-source data. Conclusions This scoping review provides a multipathogen, cross-country mapping of data sources for respiratory virus surveillance and research in Europe over 2 decades, applying an innovative objective-driven framework. Unlike prior reviews focused on single pathogens or data types, it offers a consolidated, comparative perspective based on 2564 reports to inform public health decision-making. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated innovation in data generation and access, but progress remained largely centered on SARS-CoV-2, while structural fragmentation continues to limit timely, integrated data across Europe. Strengthening preparedness will require interoperable infrastructures, federated analysis platforms, sustainable funding for surveillance innovations, and cross-sectoral data sharing.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 由流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 引起的急性呼吸道感染仍然是欧洲的主要公共卫生挑战。尽管针对这些病原体的 监测 系统已经很完善,但在过去 20 年中,支持 监测 和研究的数据流迅速多样化。这种不断扩大的数据格局,加上机构、部门和国家之间的碎片化,可能会限制及时的证据综合和有效的公共卫生决策。目的 本次范围界定审查旨在确定和描述过去 20 年来欧洲用于 监测 以及流感、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 研究的数据源,并检查其 进化 随着时间的推移、其与研究目标的一致性以及数据可用性和使用的地理差异。方法 我们使用目标驱动的分析框架进行了范围界定审查。MEDLINE、Web of Science 和 Embase 确定了 2005 年 1 月至 2025 年 9 月期间发表的实证报告。符合条件的报告重点关注流感、RSV 或 SARS-CoV-2,并包含来自 12 个欧洲国家的数据。临床和介入研究被排除在外。报告根据 4 个研究目标进行分类:流行病学监测、干预措施评估、疾病负担和健康结果评估,以及人口对公共卫生措施的依从性和信任度分析。数据源分为 9 类,包括 监测 系统、电子健康记录 (EHR)、登记、索赔、调查、数字、环境、综合数据集等。结果共纳入2564份实证报告。随着时间的推移,呼吸道病毒研究依赖于越来越多样化的数据流。虽然 监测 系统仍然处于核心地位,特别是在流行病学监测方面,但其相对主导地位有所下降。从 2020 年起,电子病历、登记、索赔数据、数字源以及链接或集成数据集的使用显着扩大,同时开放获取数据的使用也有所增加。数据源用途因研究目标而异:监测 数据在监测和干预评估中占主导地位;风险因素和 治疗 有效性研究中的 EHR;血清流行率 调查和公众信任分析;以及经济负担评估中的索赔数据。观察到了巨大的地理差异。北欧国家更频繁地使用链接和多源数据集,而南欧国家更频繁地依赖开放访问或单一来源数据。结论 本次范围界定审查应用创新的目标驱动框架,为呼吸道病毒 监测 和欧洲 20 年来的研究提供了多病原体、跨国数据源图谱。与之前专注于单一病原体或数据类型的审查不同,它提供了基于 2564 份报告的综合比较视角,为公共卫生决策提供信息。COVID-19 大流行加速了数据生成和获取方面的创新,但进展仍然主要集中在 SARS-CoV-2 上,而结构碎片化继续限制整个欧洲及时、整合的数据。加强准备工作需要可互操作的基础设施、联合分析平台、监测 创新的可持续资金以及跨部门数据共享。

title: Bridging the Vaccine Gap: Scientific and Technological Advances for Diseases Lacking Effective Vaccines.
abstract: Despite remarkable achievements in infectious disease control, more than 20 major pathogens responsible for significant global morbidity and mortality remain without licensed, effective vaccines. This so-called 'vaccine gap' disproportionately burdens low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), exacerbating health inequities and threatening global pandemic preparedness. This review comprehensively examines scientific and technological advances that are actively bridging the vaccine gap, with emphasis on novel platform technologies, immunological innovations, and translational strategies. We conducted a systematic narrative review of literature published between 2015 and 2024, encompassing peer-reviewed articles, WHO reports, clinical trial registries, and regulatory agency databases. Six transformative technology clusters were identified: (1) mRNA and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms enabling rapid antigen production; (2) viral-vectored vaccines with improved immune breadth; (3) structure-guided antigen design using cryo-electron microscopy and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven protein engineering; (4) broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies as surrogate vaccine benchmarks; (5) mucosal and inhalable delivery systems targeting tissue-resident immunity; and (6) combination adjuvant systems amplifying magnitude and durability of protective responses. Clinical translation is exemplified by candidates against HIV-1, tuberculosis (TB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants, and Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Convergence of AI-assisted rational antigen design, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvant-delivery pairings represents a paradigm shift toward vaccinatable diseases previously considered intractable. Equitable access frameworks and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain critical unresolved challenges.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the persistent 'vaccine gap' for over 20 major pathogens causing significant global morbidity and mortality, particularly affecting LMICs. It systematically evaluates advances from 2015 to 2024, identifying six transformative vaccine technology clusters: mRNA and self-amplifying RNA platforms, viral-vectored vaccines, AI-driven antigen design, broadly neutralising antibodies, mucosal delivery systems, and combination adjuvants. Clinical translation is highlighted in HIV-1, tuberculosis, RSV in infants, and malaria. However, equitable access and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain unresolved challenges. The convergence of AI, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvants signals a paradigm shift toward tackling previously intractable diseases.

title_zh: 弥合 疫苗 差距:针对缺乏有效 疫苗 的疾病的科学技术进步。
source_body_en: Despite remarkable achievements in infectious disease control, more than 20 major pathogens responsible for significant global morbidity and mortality remain without licensed, effective vaccines. This so-called 'vaccine gap' disproportionately burdens low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), exacerbating health inequities and threatening global pandemic preparedness. This review comprehensively examines scientific and technological advances that are actively bridging the vaccine gap, with emphasis on novel platform technologies, immunological innovations, and translational strategies. We conducted a systematic narrative review of literature published between 2015 and 2024, encompassing peer-reviewed articles, WHO reports, clinical trial registries, and regulatory agency databases. Six transformative technology clusters were identified: (1) mRNA and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms enabling rapid antigen production; (2) viral-vectored vaccines with improved immune breadth; (3) structure-guided antigen design using cryo-electron microscopy and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven protein engineering; (4) broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies as surrogate vaccine benchmarks; (5) mucosal and inhalable delivery systems targeting tissue-resident immunity; and (6) combination adjuvant systems amplifying magnitude and durability of protective responses. Clinical translation is exemplified by candidates against HIV-1, tuberculosis (TB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants, and Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Convergence of AI-assisted rational antigen design, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvant-delivery pairings represents a paradigm shift toward vaccinatable diseases previously considered intractable. Equitable access frameworks and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain critical unresolved challenges.
abstract_zh: 尽管在传染病控制方面取得了显著成就,但造成全球重大发病率的 20 多种主要病原体和 死亡率 仍然没有获得许可、有效的 疫苗。这种所谓的“疫苗 差距”给低收入和中等收入国家(LMIC)带来了不成比例的负担,加剧了卫生不平等并威胁到全球大流行病的防范。这篇综述全面审视了积极弥合 疫苗 差距的科学和技术进步,重点关注新颖的平台技术、免疫学创新和转化策略。我们对 2015 年至 2024 年间发表的文献进行了系统的叙述性回顾,包括同行评审文章、世界卫生组织报告、临床试验登记和监管机构数据库。确定了六大变革性技术集群:(1) mRNA 和自扩增 RNA (saRNA) 平台,可实现快速抗原生产;(2) 病毒载体疫苗,具有改善的免疫广度;(3)利用冷冻电子显微镜和人工智能(AI)驱动的蛋白质工程进行结构引导的抗原设计;(4) 广泛中和单克隆抗体作为替代 疫苗 基准;(5) 针对组织驻留免疫的粘膜和吸入递送系统;(6) 组合佐剂系统,增强保护反应的强度和持久性。临床转化的例子包括针对 HIV-1、结核病 (TB)、婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和恶性疟原虫疟疾的候选药物。人工智能辅助的合理抗原设计、下一代 mRNA 平台和创新的佐剂递送配对的融合代表着向以前被认为难以治愈的可疫苗接种疾病的范式转变。中低收入国家的公平准入框架和监管协调仍然是尚未解决的重大挑战。

title: From triplex to tetraplex: evaluation of the diagnostic accuracy of the new Roche Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B & RSV assay
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid and accurate diagnostics of epidemic respiratory viruses are relevant for optimal care pathways. In this observational diagnostic accuracy study, the novel Cobas Liat assay (Roche Molecular Systems) was evaluated for the detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the clinical setting of Tampere University Hospital, Tampere, Finland. In addition, the added value of the tetraplex assay instead of two partially overlapping triplex assays (influenza A/B and SARS-CoV-2 or RSV) was assessed in the context of adult and pediatric emergency department (AED, PED) point-of-care (PoC) testing environments. A total of 315 clinical nasopharyngeal swab samples were analyzed. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated against a molecular diagnostic reference. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had sensitivities and specificities of 100% and 98.5% for influenza A, 100% and 99.7% for influenza B, 100% and 98.2% for SARS-CoV-2, and 100% and 97.0% for RSV, respectively. Among the index and reference tests, the Cobas Liat assay demonstrated the highest analytical sensitivity for influenza A, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. No cross-reactivity with off-panel microbes was observed. With respect to clinical applicability, implementation of the evaluated tetraplex test would decrease double testing with two triplex tests in PED, likely decreasing costs and hands-on work. In AED, tetraplex testing would likely significantly increase the diagnostic yield for RSV, only rarely covered by PoC testing in AED. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had excellent clinical and analytical accuracy, being highly suitable for PoC use but also for laboratory-based testing of influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. IMPORTANCE Until recently, rapid point-of-care diagnostics have been somewhat limited by triplex four-channel analysis technology, separating four of the most important epidemic respiratory viruses—influenza A, influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus, and SARS-CoV-2—into two individual triplex tests. The evaluated tetraplex respiratory viral assay combines the two partially overlapping tests into a single test, streamlining analysis in two-test settings and potentially reducing diagnostic gaps in one-test settings. To our knowledge, this is the first study to describe the diagnostic accuracy of the novel Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) assay with additional considerations for analytical sensitivity and specificity, and clinical utility in adult and pediatric emergency department use.

In this observational diagnostic accuracy study, the novel Cobas Liat assay (Roche Molecular Systems) was evaluated for the detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the clinical setting of Tampere University Hospital, Tampere, Finland. In addition, the added value of the tetraplex assay instead of two partially overlapping triplex assays (influenza A/B and SARS-CoV-2 or RSV) was assessed in the context of adult and pediatric emergency department (AED, PED) point-of-care (PoC) testing environments. A total of 315 clinical nasopharyngeal swab samples were analyzed. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated against a molecular diagnostic reference. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had sensitivities and specificities of 100% and 98.5% for influenza A, 100% and 99.7% for influenza B, 100% and 98.2% for SARS-CoV-2, and 100% and 97.0% for RSV, respectively. Among the index and reference tests, the Cobas Liat assay demonstrated the highest analytical sensitivity for influenza A, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV. No cross-reactivity with off-panel microbes was observed. With respect to clinical applicability, implementation of the evaluated tetraplex test would decrease double testing with two triplex tests in PED, likely decreasing costs and hands-on work. In AED, tetraplex testing would likely significantly increase the diagnostic yield for RSV, only rarely covered by PoC testing in AED. The evaluated Cobas Liat assay had excellent clinical and analytical accuracy, being highly suitable for PoC use but also for laboratory-based testing of influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV.IMPORTANCEUntil recently, rapid point-of-care diagnostics have been somewhat limited by triplex four-channel analysis technology, separating four of the most important epidemic respiratory viruses-influenza A, influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus, and SARS-CoV-2-into two individual triplex tests. The evaluated tetraplex respiratory viral assay combines the two partially overlapping tests into a single test, streamlining analysis in two-test settings and potentially reducing diagnostic gaps in one-test settings. To our knowledge, this is the first study to describe the diagnostic accuracy of the novel Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) assay with additional considerations for analytical sensitivity and specificity, and clinical utility in adult and pediatric emergency department use.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rapid and accurate diagnostics for epidemic respiratory viruses are critical for optimal care pathways, but rapid point-of-care testing has been limited by triplex technology that separates key viruses into overlapping assays. The study addressed the need for a single tetraplex assay to streamline testing and reduce diagnostic gaps.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the novel Cobas Liat tetraplex assay (Roche Molecular Systems) for detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV in Tampere University Hospital, Finland. A total of 315 clinical nasopharyngeal swab samples were analyzed in adult and pediatric emergency department point-of-care settings.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic accuracy was assessed against a molecular diagnostic reference. The study evaluated the added value of the tetraplex assay compared to two partially overlapping triplex assays in point-of-care testing environments. Analytical sensitivity and specificity were determined for each virus.
analysis.main_results: The Cobas Liat assay demonstrated sensitivities and specificities of 100% and 98.5% for influenza A, 100% and 99.7% for influenza B, 100% and 98.2% for SARS-CoV-2, and 100% and 97.0% for RSV, respectively. No cross-reactivity with off-panel microbes was observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The tetraplex assay showed excellent clinical and analytical accuracy, being highly suitable for point-of-care and laboratory-based testing. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to describe the diagnostic accuracy of the novel Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV assay with considerations for analytical sensitivity, specificity, and clinical utility in emergency department settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Implementation of the tetraplex test would decrease double testing with two triplex tests in pediatric emergency departments, likely reducing costs and hands-on work. In adult emergency departments, tetraplex testing would likely increase the diagnostic yield for RSV, which is rarely covered by point-of-care testing.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single hospital setting with a limited sample size of 315 nasopharyngeal swabs, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is derived from an observational diagnostic accuracy study without randomization, limiting causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This observational diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the novel Roche Cobas Liat tetraplex assay for detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and RSV in Tampere University Hospital, Finland. The assay demonstrated perfect sensitivity (100%) and high specificity (97.0%–99.7%) for all viruses tested, with no cross-reactivity observed. The tetraplex format streamlines testing by combining two overlapping triplex assays into a single test, reducing double testing and hands-on work in pediatric emergency departments and increasing RSV diagnostic yield in adult emergency departments. The study is the first to assess the assay's diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility in emergency department point-of-care settings, highlighting its potential for improving respiratory virus diagnostics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流行性呼吸道病毒的快速、准确诊断对于最佳护理途径至关重要,但快速护理点检测受到三重技术的限制,该技术将关键病毒分离到重叠的检测中。该研究解决了对单一四重检测的需求,以简化测试并减少诊断差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项观察性诊断准确性研究评估了芬兰坦佩雷大学医院用于检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 的新型 Cobas Liat 四联检测(罗氏分子系统)。在成人和儿童急诊科护理点环境中对总共 315 份临床鼻咽拭子样本进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 根据分子诊断参考评估诊断准确性。该研究评估了四重检测与在护理点测试环境中两个部分重叠的三重检测相比的附加价值。确定了每种病毒的分析灵敏度和特异性。
elements_zh.main_results: Cobas Liat 检测显示,甲型流感的敏感性和特异性分别为 100% 和 98.5%,乙型流感为 100% 和 99.7%,SARS-CoV-2 为 100% 和 98.2%,RSV 为 100% 和 97.0%。未观察到与面板外微生物的交叉反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 四重检测显示出出色的临床和分析准确性,非常适合现场护理和实验室测试。据作者所知,这是第一项描述新型 Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 检测的诊断准确性的研究,同时考虑了分析灵敏度、特异性和在急诊科环境中的临床实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四重测试的实施将减少儿科急诊科中两次三重测试的双重测试,可能会降低成本和实际工作。在成人急诊科,四重检测可能会提高 RSV 的诊断率,而护理点检测很少涵盖 RSV。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家医院环境中进行的,样本量有限,只有 315 份鼻咽拭子,这可能会影响普适性。证据来自观察性诊断准确性研究,没有随机化,限制了因果推断。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 流行性呼吸道病毒的快速、准确诊断对于最佳护理途径至关重要,但快速护理点检测受到三重技术的限制,该技术将关键病毒分离到重叠的检测中。该研究解决了对单一四重检测的需求,以简化测试并减少诊断差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项观察性诊断准确性研究评估了芬兰坦佩雷大学医院用于检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 的新型 Cobas Liat 四联检测(罗氏分子系统)。在成人和儿童急诊科护理点环境中对总共 315 份临床鼻咽拭子样本进行了分析。
analysis_zh.methods: 根据分子诊断参考评估诊断准确性。该研究评估了四重检测与在护理点测试环境中两个部分重叠的三重检测相比的附加价值。确定了每种病毒的分析灵敏度和特异性。
analysis_zh.main_results: Cobas Liat 检测显示,甲型流感的敏感性和特异性分别为 100% 和 98.5%,乙型流感为 100% 和 99.7%,SARS-CoV-2 为 100% 和 98.2%,RSV 为 100% 和 97.0%。未观察到与面板外微生物的交叉反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 四重检测显示出出色的临床和分析准确性,非常适合现场护理和实验室测试。据作者所知,这是第一项描述新型 Cobas Liat SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感和 RSV 检测的诊断准确性的研究,同时考虑了分析灵敏度、特异性和在急诊科环境中的临床实用性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四重测试的实施将减少儿科急诊科中两次三重测试的双重测试,可能会降低成本和实际工作。在成人急诊科,四重检测可能会提高 RSV 的诊断率,而护理点检测很少涵盖 RSV。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家医院环境中进行的,样本量有限,只有 315 份鼻咽拭子,这可能会影响普适性。证据来自观察性诊断准确性研究,没有随机化,限制了因果推断。

title: Clesrovimab in Infants at Increased Risk For Severe Disease During 2 RSV Seasons
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Clesrovimab is a long-acting monoclonal antibody approved for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season; data concerning clesrovimab from a second RSV season among children who remain at risk for severe disease are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of clesrovimab (105 mg) vs palivizumab in RSV season 1 in infants at increased risk for severe RSV disease. Key secondary objectives include describing the safety of 210 mg of clesrovimab in RSV season 2 in children who remain at increased risk for severe RSV disease, clesrovimab pharmacokinetics, and the incidence of RSV-associated disease. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: SMART (MK-1654-007) was a randomized, partially masked, palivizumab-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial, conducted at 110 sites in 27 countries and territories between November 30, 2021, and November 20, 2025. The population constituted palivizumab-eligible infants, including those with prematurity, chronic lung disease of prematurity, or hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease. INTERVENTIONS: Participants, randomized 1:1 and stratified by region and condition, received clesrovimab (105 mg) on day 1 followed by placebo on day 28 or monthly palivizumab (15 mg/kg) up to 5 doses (1 dose per month). Eligible infants received open-label clesrovimab (210 mg) before their second RSV season. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the observed proportions of participants experiencing adverse events (AEs) after clesrovimab or palivizumab in season 1. RESULTS: Overall, 997 infants (500 [50.2%] male; median age, 2.6 [range, 0.0-12.0] months) received clesrovimab, 105 mg (n = 498) or palivizumab (n = 499) in season 1; 276 received clesrovimab, 210 mg open-label in season 2. In season 1, the proportions of participants experiencing AEs were comparable between treatment groups. In season 2, clesrovimab, 210 mg was well tolerated. Incidence rates of RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection (MALRI) were comparable between clesrovimab and palivizumab (3.2% [95% CI, 1.8%-5.2%] and 3.4% [95% CI, 2.0%-5.6%], respectively) through day 150 in season 1; total RSV-associated MALRI incidence through day 180 after a 210-mg dose in season 2 was 7.3% (95% CI, 4.4%-11.4%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, clesrovimab was well tolerated in infants at increased risk for severe RSV disease through 2 RSV seasons. These findings support the use of clesrovimab in children who remain at risk for severe RSV disease in their second RSV season. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04938830.

analysis.summary_en: This randomized, partially masked, phase 3 trial (SMART MK-1654-007) evaluated the safety and tolerability of clesrovimab versus palivizumab in infants at increased risk for severe RSV disease across two RSV seasons. Conducted at 110 sites in 27 countries from 2021 to 2025, the study enrolled palivizumab-eligible infants with prematurity, chronic lung disease, or congenital heart disease. Participants received clesrovimab (105 mg) or monthly palivizumab (15 mg/kg) in season 1, with open-label clesrovimab (210 mg) administered before season 2. The primary outcome was adverse events in season 1, while secondary objectives included safety in season 2 and incidence of RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection. Results showed comparable adverse event rates between groups in season 1 and acceptable tolerability of clesrovimab in season 2. Incidence of RSV-associated disease was similar between clesrovimab and palivizumab in season 1 (3.2% vs 3.4%) and 7.3% in season 2 after a 210-mg dose. The study concludes that clesrovimab is well tolerated through two RSV seasons, supporting its use in high-risk infants during their second season.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 会导致婴儿严重的下呼吸道疾病,并且缺乏第一个 RSV 季节之后的 clesrovimab 的长期安全性数据。该研究需要评估 clesrovimab 对于在第二个 RSV 季节期间风险仍然增加的婴儿是否仍然安全有效。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: SMART(MK-1654-007)是一项随机、部分掩蔽、帕利珠单抗对照的 3 期临床试验,于 2021 年 11 月 30 日至 2025 年 11 月 20 日期间在 27 个国家和地区的 110 个地点进行。参与者是符合帕利珠单抗资格的婴儿,包括患有早产儿、早产儿慢性肺病或血流动力学显着先天性心脏病的婴儿。
elements_zh.methods: 参与者按 1:1 比例随机分组,并按地区和病情分层,在第 1 天接受 clesrovimab (105 mg),然后在第 28 天接受安慰剂,或每月接受帕利珠单抗 (15 mg/kg),最多 5 剂。符合条件的婴儿在第二个 RSV 季节之前接受开放标签 clesrovimab(210 毫克)。主要结局是在第一季中观察到的接受 clesrovimab 或 palivizumab 治疗后出现不良事件的参与者比例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在两个 RSV 季节中,患有严重 RSV 疾病风险增加的婴儿中,Clesrovimab 具有良好的耐受性,RSV 相关疾病的安全性和 发病率 与第 1 季的帕利珠单抗相当,并且在第 2 季的耐受性可接受。该研究提供了新的证据,支持在第二个 RSV 季节仍处于风险中的儿童中使用 clesrovimab。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持使用clesrovimab来预防在第二个RSV季节风险增加的婴儿中RSV相关的下呼吸道疾病,提供帕利珠单抗的长效替代品。

RESULTS: Overall, 997 infants (500 [50.2%] male; median age, 2.6 [range, 0.0-12.0] months) received clesrovimab, 105 mg (n = 498) or palivizumab (n = 499) in season 1; 276 received clesrovimab, 210 mg open-label in season 2. In season 1, the proportions of participants experiencing AEs were comparable between treatment groups. In season 2, clesrovimab, 210 mg was well tolerated. Incidence rates of RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection (MALRI) were comparable between clesrovimab and palivizumab (3.2% [95% CI, 1.8%-5.2%] and 3.4% [95% CI, 2.0%-5.6%], respectively) through day 150 in season 1; total RSV-associated MALRI incidence through day 180 after a 210-mg dose in season 2 was 7.3% (95% CI, 4.4%-11.4%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, clesrovimab was well tolerated in infants at increased risk for severe RSV disease through 2 RSV seasons. These findings support the use of clesrovimab in children who remain at risk for severe RSV disease in their second RSV season. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04938830.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 会导致婴儿严重的下呼吸道疾病,并且缺乏第一个 RSV 季节之后的 clesrovimab 的长期安全性数据。该研究需要评估 clesrovimab 对于在第二个 RSV 季节期间风险仍然增加的婴儿是否仍然安全有效。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: SMART(MK-1654-007)是一项随机、部分掩蔽、帕利珠单抗对照的 3 期临床试验,于 2021 年 11 月 30 日至 2025 年 11 月 20 日期间在 27 个国家和地区的 110 个地点进行。参与者是符合帕利珠单抗资格的婴儿,包括患有早产儿、早产儿慢性肺病或血流动力学显着先天性心脏病的婴儿。
analysis_zh.methods: 参与者按 1:1 比例随机分组,并按地区和病情分层,在第 1 天接受 clesrovimab (105 mg),然后在第 28 天接受安慰剂,或每月接受帕利珠单抗 (15 mg/kg),最多 5 剂。符合条件的婴儿在第二个 RSV 季节之前接受开放标签 clesrovimab(210 毫克)。主要结局是在第一季中观察到的接受 clesrovimab 或 palivizumab 治疗后出现不良事件的参与者比例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在两个 RSV 季节中,患有严重 RSV 疾病风险增加的婴儿中,Clesrovimab 具有良好的耐受性,RSV 相关疾病的安全性和 发病率 与第 1 季的帕利珠单抗相当,并且在第 2 季的耐受性可接受。该研究提供了新的证据,支持在第二个 RSV 季节仍处于风险中的儿童中使用 clesrovimab。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持使用clesrovimab来预防在第二个RSV季节风险增加的婴儿中RSV相关的下呼吸道疾病,提供帕利珠单抗的长效替代品。

title: CAUSAL-RSV: Causal Analysis of RSV Vaccine Effects in Infants Using Real-World Data
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) contributes to substantial morbidity and mortality in young children each year. In 2023, two new prevention products were licensed and recommended in the United States (US), including a prefusion F protein subunit vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered in infants. Although post-licensure real-world studies support the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine during pregnancy, existing studies have been conducted in settings where only RSVpreF vaccine is available. The real-world effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in settings where both RSVpreF vaccine and mAbs are available is not yet well understood. The goal of this study is to estimate the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV by applying causal mediation analysis with receipt of mAbs as a mediating variable. Using a national cohort of mother-infant dyads with the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW), we will model vaccine and mAb effects in a longitudinal cohort spanning the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 RSV seasons. Results will be used to better understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination when it is used as one component within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant morbidity and mortality in young children, and in 2023 two new prevention products were licensed in the US: a prefusion F protein subunit vaccine (RSVpreF) given during pregnancy and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered to infants. Existing real-world studies have evaluated RSVpreF effectiveness only in settings where the mAb was unavailable, leaving a knowledge gap regarding its effectiveness in hybrid prevention programs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a national cohort of mother-infant dyads from the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW) to model vaccine and mAb effects across three RSV seasons (2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26).
analysis.methods: The study applied causal mediation analysis with receipt of mAbs as a mediating variable to estimate the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV.
analysis.main_results: Results will be used to better understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination when it is used as one component within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors aim to interpret the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program, addressing a gap in understanding how the vaccine performs when both RSVpreF and mAbs are available.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings are expected to inform public health strategies for RSV prevention in infants by clarifying the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination in settings where monoclonal antibodies are also used.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to an abstract-only report, which lacks detailed methods, results, and discussion, resulting in a low confidence assessment due to the absence of empirical data and methodological transparency.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV in settings where both RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and long-acting monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for infants are available. Using a national cohort of mother-infant dyads from the Optum Labs Data Warehouse across three RSV seasons (2023-24 to 2025-26), the authors applied causal mediation analysis with mAb receipt as a mediating variable to estimate vaccine effectiveness. The goal is to understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination within a hybrid prevention program. However, the evidence is limited to an abstract, which does not report numerical results, statistical outputs, or detailed methodological descriptions, resulting in low confidence in the findings.

title_zh: CAUSAL-RSV:使用真实世界数据对 RSV 疫苗 对婴儿的影响进行因果分析
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) contributes to substantial morbidity and mortality in young children each year. In 2023, two new prevention products were licensed and recommended in the United States (US), including a prefusion F protein subunit vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy and a long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered in infants. Although post-licensure real-world studies support the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine during pregnancy, existing studies have been conducted in settings where only RSVpreF vaccine is available. The real-world effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in settings where both RSVpreF vaccine and mAbs are available is not yet well understood. The goal of this study is to estimate the real-world effectiveness of the RSVpreF vaccine against severe infant RSV by applying causal mediation analysis with receipt of mAbs as a mediating variable. Using a national cohort of mother-infant dyads with the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW), we will model vaccine and mAb effects in a longitudinal cohort spanning the 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 RSV seasons. Results will be used to better understand the total effect of RSVpreF vaccination when it is used as one component within a hybrid infant RSV prevention program.

title: Optimization of the antiviral spectrum of cyclophilin inhibitors targeting respiratory viruses.
abstract: ABSTRACT We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Structure–spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. By combining the key determinants identified for each virus, we rationally designed optimized dual-acting derivatives. Among these, the optimized compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum antiviral agent with nanomolar activity against both hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin (Cyp) peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (PPIase) activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Interestingly, no direct correlation was observed between Cyp PPIase inhibition and antiviral potency, suggesting that Cyp engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition per se is required for antiviral activity. Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure–activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need for broad-spectrum antivirals against respiratory viruses with limited treatment options, specifically targeting human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). The authors aimed to optimize cyclophilin inhibitors to expand their antiviral spectrum beyond existing narrow-spectrum activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against hRSV and hMPV using structure–spectrum analysis and rational design. The optimized compound F832/33 was tested for antiviral activity, cyclophilin inhibition, and cytotoxicity in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells.
analysis.methods: The authors performed structure–activity relationship-guided optimization to identify key determinants for antiviral efficacy against hRSV and hMPV. Antiviral potency was assessed using nanomolar and submicromolar inhibition assays, while cytotoxicity was evaluated. Competition assays with alisporivir were used to confirm the dependence of antiviral effects on cyclophilin interaction.
analysis.main_results: The optimized compound F832/33 demonstrated nanomolar activity against hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. No direct correlation was observed between cyclophilin enzymatic inhibition and antiviral potency. F832/33 also showed strong antiviral activity against parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron SARS-CoV-2 strains in cell models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that cyclophilin engagement, rather than enzymatic inhibition, is critical for antiviral activity, highlighting a novel mechanism for broad-spectrum antiviral development. The study demonstrates that rational design can successfully expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted candidate.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that F832/33 could serve as a broad-spectrum antiviral for multiple respiratory pathogens, addressing unmet needs in treatment options. The host-targeted mechanism may reduce resistance development and provide a platform for optimizing antivirals against emerging respiratory viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro and cell-based models, with no in vivo data provided. The study relies on abstract-level evidence, and further preclinical and clinical evaluations are needed to confirm therapeutic potential and mechanism of action.

analysis.summary_en: This study optimized urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) to broaden their antiviral spectrum against respiratory viruses. By evaluating 36 compounds against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), the authors identified structural requirements for antiviral efficacy and rationally designed the dual-acting derivative F832/33. The compound exhibited nanomolar antiviral activity against hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar cyclophilin inhibition, and no cytotoxicity, while also demonstrating activity against parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and SARS-CoV-2 variants. Mechanistic studies suggested that cyclophilin engagement, rather than enzymatic inhibition, drives antiviral effects. The findings highlight a novel host-targeted approach for broad-spectrum antivirals, though further in vivo studies are required to validate therapeutic potential.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了对广谱 抗病毒药物 对抗呼吸道病毒的需求,但 治疗 的选择有限,特别针对人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV)。作者旨在优化亲环蛋白抑制剂,以将其 抗病毒药物 谱扩展到现有的窄谱活性之外。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用结构谱分析和合理设计评估了 36 种基于尿素的小分子亲环蛋白抑制剂 (SMCypIs) 对抗 hRSV 和 hMPV 的库。在永生化细胞系和完全分化的人鼻上皮细胞中测试了优化的化合物 F832/33 的 抗病毒药物 活性、亲环蛋白抑制和细胞毒性。
elements_zh.methods: 作者进行了结构-活性关系引导的优化,以确定 抗病毒药物 对 hRSV 和 hMPV 功效的关键决定因素。使用纳摩尔和亚微摩尔抑制测定评估抗病毒药物的效力,同时评估细胞毒性。使用阿拉泊韦的竞争测定来确认 抗病毒药物 效应对亲环蛋白相互作用的依赖性。
elements_zh.main_results: 优化的化合物 F832/33 对 hRSV 和 hMPV 表现出纳摩尔级活性,对亲环蛋白肽基脯氨酰异构酶活性具有亚微摩尔级抑制作用,且未检测到细胞毒性。在亲环蛋白酶抑制和 抗病毒药物 效力之间没有观察到直接相关性。F832/33 在细胞模型中还对副流感病毒 3 型、肠道病毒 D68 以及祖先和 Omicron SARS-CoV-2 株表现出强大的 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,亲环蛋白的参与,而不是酶的抑制,对 抗病毒药物 活性至关重要,突出了广谱 抗病毒药物 开发的新机制。该研究表明,合理的设计可以成功扩展 SMCypIs 的 抗病毒药物 谱,将 F832/33 定位为有前途的 宿主 靶向候选药物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,F832/33 可以作为针对多种呼吸道病原体的广谱 抗病毒药物,解决 治疗 选项中未满足的需求。宿主 靶向机制可以减少耐药性的发展,并为优化 抗病毒药物 针对新兴呼吸道病毒提供平台。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外和基于细胞的模型,没有提供体内数据。该研究依赖于抽象水平的证据,需要进一步的临床前和临床评估来确认治疗潜力和作用机制。

title_zh: 针对呼吸道病毒的亲环蛋白抑制剂 抗病毒药物 谱的优化。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT We evaluated the antiviral activity of a library of 36 urea-based small-molecule cyclophilin inhibitors (SMCypIs) against human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV). Structure–spectrum analysis revealed virus-specific structural requirements for antiviral efficacy. By combining the key determinants identified for each virus, we rationally designed optimized dual-acting derivatives. Among these, the optimized compound F832/33 emerged as a potent, broad-spectrum antiviral agent with nanomolar activity against both hRSV and hMPV, submicromolar inhibition of cyclophilin (Cyp) peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (PPIase) activity, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Interestingly, no direct correlation was observed between Cyp PPIase inhibition and antiviral potency, suggesting that Cyp engagement rather than enzymatic inhibition per se is required for antiviral activity. Competition assays with alisporivir confirmed that the antiviral effects of SMCypIs depend on their specific interaction with Cyp. Beyond its dual efficacy, F832/33 displayed strong antiviral activity against additional clinically relevant respiratory pathogens, including parainfluenza virus type 3, enterovirus D68, and both ancestral and Omicron severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 strains, in immortalized cell lines and fully differentiated human nasal epithelial cells, a physiologically relevant model of respiratory infection. Collectively, our results demonstrate that structure–activity relationship-guided optimization can be successfully applied to expand the antiviral spectrum of SMCypIs, positioning F832/33 as a promising host-targeted broad-spectrum antiviral candidate. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its therapeutic potential and clarify its precise mechanism of action.
abstract_zh: 摘要 我们评估了 36 种基于尿素的小分子亲环蛋白抑制剂 (SMCypIs) 文库针对人 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的 抗病毒药物 活性。结构谱分析揭示了 抗病毒药物 功效的病毒特异性结构要求。通过结合每种病毒确定的关键决定因素,我们合理地设计了优化的双作用衍生物。其中,优化的化合物 F832/33 成为一种有效的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物,对 hRSV 和 hMPV 具有纳摩尔级活性,对亲环蛋白 (Cyp) 肽基脯氨酰异构酶 (PPIase) 活性具有亚微摩尔级抑制作用,并且没有可检测到的细胞毒性。有趣的是,在 Cyp PPIase 抑制和 抗病毒药物 效力之间没有观察到直接相关性,这表明 抗病毒药物 活性需要 Cyp 参与而不是酶抑制本身。使用阿拉泊韦的竞争测定证实,SMCypIs 的 抗病毒药物 效应取决于它们与 Cyp 的特异性相互作用。除了其双重功效之外,F832/33 在永生化细胞系和完全分化的人鼻上皮细胞(一种生理相关的呼吸道感染模型)中,对其他临床相关呼吸道病原体(包括副流感病毒 3 型、肠道病毒 D68 以及祖先和 Omicron 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 株)表现出强大的 抗病毒药物 活性。总的来说,我们的结果表明,结构-活性关系引导的优化可以成功地应用于扩展 SMCypIs 的 抗病毒药物 谱,将 F832/33 定位为有前途的 宿主 靶向广谱 抗病毒药物 候选药物。需要进一步的体内研究来评估其治疗潜力并阐明其精确的作用机制。
